sentences.zh: 桑喬，字子木，江都人。

translations.literal: Sang Qiao, style Zimu, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Qiao, styled Zimu, came from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，由主事改御史，出按山西。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year, from department director he was changed to censor and went out to inspect Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year he was transferred from department director to censor and sent to inspect Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 所部頻寇躪，喬奏請盡蠲徭賦，厚恤死者家。

translations.literal: The districts under his jurisdiction were repeatedly overrun by bandits; Qiao memorialized asking that corvée levies be entirely remitted and the families of the dead generously compensated.
translations.idiomatic: The regions under his jurisdiction were repeatedly ravaged by bandits; Qiao memorialized asking that corvée levies be remitted entirely and the families of the dead generously relieved.

sentences.zh: 參將葉宗等將萬人至荊家莊，陷賊伏中，大潰，賊遂深入。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Ye Zong and others led ten thousand men to Jingjiazhuang, fell into an enemy ambush, and were routed in great disorder; the bandits then drove deep inland.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Ye Zong and others led ten thousand men to Jingjiazhuang, walked into an enemy ambush, and were routed; the bandits then pushed deep into the interior.

sentences.zh: 天城、陽和兩月間五遭寇。

translations.literal: Tiancheng and Yanghe within two months suffered five raids by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng and Yanghe suffered five bandit raids within two months.

sentences.zh: 巡撫樊繼祖、總兵官魯綱以下，皆為喬劾，副將李懋及宗等六人並逮治。

translations.literal: The Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu, the supreme commander Lu Gang, and those below them were all impeached by Qiao; Vice Commander Li Mao and Zong and six others were all arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu, supreme commander Lu Gang, and their subordinates were all impeached by Qiao; Vice Commander Li Mao and Zong and six others were arrested and punished together.

sentences.zh: 十六年夏，雷震謹身殿，下詔求言。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixteenth year, lightning struck the Hall of Cultivation and an edict was issued seeking remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixteenth year lightning struck the Hall of Cultivation, and the throne issued an edict calling for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 喬偕同官陳三事，略言營造兩宮山陵，多侵冒；

translations.literal: Qiao together with his colleagues submitted three matters, briefly stating that in constructing the two palaces and the imperial tombs there was much embezzlement;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao and his colleagues memorialized on three matters, noting briefly that construction of the two palaces and the imperial tombs involved much embezzlement;

sentences.zh: 吉囊恣橫，邊備積弛。

translations.literal: the Jinang acted wantonly and border defenses had long grown slack.
translations.idiomatic: the Jinang were running rampant and border defenses had long been neglected.

sentences.zh: 而末言：「陛下遇災而懼，下詔修省。

translations.literal: At the end he said: "Your Majesty, encountering this calamity, became fearful and issued an edict for self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he said: "Your Majesty, meeting this calamity, became fearful and issued an edict for self-examination.

sentences.zh: 修省不外人事，人事無過擇官。

translations.literal: Self-examination is nothing outside human affairs, and in human affairs nothing surpasses choosing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Self-examination lies in human affairs alone, and among human affairs nothing surpasses choosing officials.

sentences.zh: 尚書嚴嵩及林庭㭿、張瓚、張雲皆上負國恩，下乖輿望，災變之來，由彼所致。」

translations.literal: The Ministers Yan Song and Lin Tingzhen, Zhang Zan, and Zhang Yun all bear the state's grace above while below they oppose public expectation; the coming of portents was caused by them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Yan Song, Lin Tingzhen, Zhang Zan, and Zhang Yun all fail the state's grace above and betray public expectation below; these portents have come because of them.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，四人皆乞罷。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, all four men begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, all four men asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 詔庭㭿、雲致仕，留嵩、瓚如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tingzhen and Yun to retire, while Song and Zan were kept as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Tingzhen and Yun to retire while Song and Zan were kept in office as before.

sentences.zh: 嵩再疏辨，且詆言者。

translations.literal: Song memorialized again in defense and also slandered those who spoke out.
translations.idiomatic: Song memorialized again in his own defense and also vilified those who had spoken out.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡汝霖言：「大臣被論，引罪求退而已。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Hu Rulin said: "When a great minister is impeached, he admits guilt and seeks withdrawal—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hu Rulin said: "When a great minister is impeached, he should admit guilt and seek withdrawal—that is all.

sentences.zh: 嵩負穢行，召物議，逞辭奏辨，陰擠言官，無大臣體。」

translations.literal: Song bears a filthy record, invites public censure, yet vaunts his words in memorials of defense and secretly undermines remonstrating officials, without the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Song bears a foul record and invites public censure, yet he vaunts his words in memorials of defense and secretly undermines remonstrating officials—he lacks the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔戒飭如汝霖指。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict of admonition along the lines Rulin indicated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued an edict of admonition along the lines Rulin had indicated.

sentences.zh: 時嵩拜尚書甫半歲，方養交遊，揚聲譽，為進取地，舉朝猶未知其奸，喬獨首發之。

translations.literal: At that time Song had been Minister for only half a year and was still cultivating connections and raising his reputation to pave the way for advancement; the whole court still did not know his treachery—Qiao alone was first to expose it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Song had been Minister for only half a year and was still cultivating connections and burnishing his reputation to advance; the whole court still did not know his treachery—Qiao alone was the first to expose it.

sentences.zh: 喬尋巡按畿輔，引疾。

translations.literal: Before long Qiao inspected the capital region and cited illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qiao inspected the capital region and cited illness.

sentences.zh: 都御史王廷相以規避劾之，嵩因構其罪。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang impeached him for evasion, and Song thereupon framed charges against him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang impeached him for evading duty, and Song thereupon framed charges against him.

sentences.zh: 逮下詔獄，廷杖，戍九江。

translations.literal: He was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, given court beating, and exiled to garrison duty at Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and exiled to garrison duty at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 居戍所二十六年而卒。

translations.literal: After twenty-six years in exile he died.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-six years in exile he died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, posthumous gifts and condolences were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign, posthumous honors and relief were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 胡汝霖，綿州人。

translations.literal: Hu Rulin was a native of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Rulin came from Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士除戶科給事中。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十年四月，九廟災。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twentieth year, the nine ancestral temples burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twentieth year the nine ancestral temples burned.

sentences.zh: 偕同官聶靜、御史李乘雲劾文武大臣救火緩慢者二十六人，嵩與焉。

translations.literal: Together with his colleague Nie Jing and the Censor Li Chengyun he impeached twenty-six civil and military great ministers for sluggishness in firefighting, Song among them.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his colleague Nie Jing and Censor Li Chengyun he impeached twenty-six civil and military great ministers for sluggish firefighting, Song among them.

sentences.zh: 帝怒所劾不盡，下詔獄訊治，俱鐫級調外。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry that those impeached were not complete and had them all sent to the imperial prison for investigation; all were demoted one grade and transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry that the impeachments were incomplete and had them all sent to the imperial prison for investigation; all were demoted one grade and transferred outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 汝霖得太平府經歷。

translations.literal: Rulin received the post of registrar of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin was assigned as registrar of Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既謫官，則請解於嵩，反附以進。

translations.literal: After his demotion he asked to be released from obligation to Song and instead attached himself to him for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: After his demotion he asked to be released from any quarrel with Song and instead attached himself to him for advancement.

sentences.zh: 累遷至右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted until Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 及嵩敗，以嵩黨奪官。

translations.literal: When Song fell, he was stripped of office as Song's partisan.
translations.idiomatic: When Song fell, he was stripped of office as a member of Song's faction.

sentences.zh: 謝瑜，字如卿，上虞人。

translations.literal: Xie Yu, style Ruqing, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yu, styled Ruqing, came from Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 由南京御史改北。

translations.literal: From Nanjing censor he was transferred to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from Nanjing censor to the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，禮部尚書嚴嵩屢被彈劾求去，帝慰留。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year, the Minister of Rites Yan Song, having repeatedly been impeached and sought to leave, was comforted and kept by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the nineteenth year Minister of Rites Yan Song, having been repeatedly impeached and asked to resign, was comforted and kept in office by the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 瑜言：「嵩矯飾浮詞，欺罔君上，箝制言官。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Song uses florid phrasing to deceive his sovereign above and muzzle remonstrating officials below.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Song dresses up empty words, deceives his sovereign above, and muzzles remonstrating officials below.

sentences.zh: 且援明堂大禮、南巡盛事為解，而謂諸臣中無為陛下任事者，欲以激聖怒。

translations.literal: Moreover he cites the great rites of the Bright Hall and the magnificent southern tour as his defense, yet says that among the officials none serves Your Majesty—that he means to provoke the sage's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he cites the Bright Hall rites and the magnificent southern tour as his defense, yet says that among the officials none truly serves Your Majesty—he means to provoke the sage ruler's anger.

sentences.zh: 奸狀顯然。」

translations.literal: His treacherous conduct is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: His treachery is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 帝留疏不下。

translations.literal: The Emperor kept the memorial and did not release it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept the memorial and did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 嵩奏辨，且言：「瑜擊臣不已，欲與朝廷爭勝」。

translations.literal: Song memorialized in defense and moreover said: "Yu has attacked your minister without cease, wishing to contend with the court for victory."
translations.idiomatic: Song memorialized in his defense and added: "Yu has attacked your minister without cease, wishing to contend with the court for victory."

sentences.zh: 帝於是切責瑜，而慰諭嵩甚至。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon sharply reproved Yu while comforting and reassuring Song to an extreme degree.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon sharply rebuked Yu while comforting and reassuring Song to an extraordinary degree.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，竟用嵩為相。

translations.literal: After two years, Song was at last made Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Song was at last made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 甫逾月，瑜疏言：「武廟盤遊佚樂，邊防宜壞而未甚壞。

translations.literal: Just over a month later, Yu memorialized saying: "Under the Martial Ancestor's court there was roaming dissipation and pleasure; border defenses were liable to collapse but had not yet collapsed severely.
translations.idiomatic: Just over a month later Yu memorialized: "Under the Martial Ancestor's court there was roaming dissipation and pleasure; the borders were liable to break down but had not yet broken down severely.

sentences.zh: 今聖明在上，邊防宜固而反大壞者，大臣謀國不忠，而陛下任用失也。

translations.literal: Now under a sage and brilliant sovereign, border defenses ought to be firm yet have instead greatly broken down—great ministers do not plan loyally for the state, and Your Majesty has erred in appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Now, under a sage and brilliant sovereign, the borders ought to be secure yet have instead collapsed—great ministers do not plan loyally for the state, and Your Majesty has erred in whom you appoint.

sentences.zh: 自張瓚為中樞，掌兵而天下無兵，擇將而天下無將。

translations.literal: Ever since Zhang Zan became head of the central military administration, though he holds command of troops there are no troops in the realm, and though he chooses generals there are no generals in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Zhang Zan became head of the central military administration, though he holds command of troops the realm has no troops, and though he chooses generals the realm has no generals.

sentences.zh: 說者謂瓚形貌魁梧，足稱福將。

translations.literal: Some say Zan's imposing stature suffices to be called a general of good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Zan's imposing stature is enough to make him a general of good fortune.

sentences.zh: 夫誠邊塵不聳，海宇晏然，謂之福可也。

translations.literal: If truly the border dust did not rise and the realm were tranquil, one might call that fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If the border alarms truly did not rise and the realm were tranquil, one might call that fortune.

sentences.zh: 今瓚無功而恩蔭屢加，有罪而褫奪不及，此其福乃一身之福，非軍國之福也。

translations.literal: Now Zan has no merit yet enfeoffment favors are repeatedly added; when guilty he is not stripped of rank and office—this fortune is fortune for his person alone, not fortune for army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zan has no merit yet enfeoffment favors are repeatedly added; when guilty he is not stripped of rank—this fortune is fortune for him alone, not fortune for army and state.

sentences.zh: 昔舜誅四兇，萬世稱聖。

translations.literal: In antiquity Shun executed the Four Malefactors and was called sage for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Shun executed the Four Malefactors and was called sage for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 今瓚與郭勛、嚴嵩、胡守中，聖世之四兇。

translations.literal: Now Zan, Guo Xun, Yan Song, and Hu Shouzhong are the Four Malefactors of the sage age.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zan, Guo Xun, Yan Song, and Hu Shouzhong are the Four Malefactors of this sage age.

sentences.zh: 陛下旬月間已誅其二，天下翕然稱聖，何不並此二兇，放之流之，以全帝舜之功也？

translations.literal: Within a fortnight Your Majesty has already executed two of them and all under heaven unanimously calls Your Majesty sage—why not deal with these two malefactors as well, banishing or exiling them, to complete the achievement of Emperor Shun?
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight Your Majesty has already executed two of them and all under heaven calls you sage—why not deal with these two malefactors as well, banishing or exiling them, to complete the achievement of Emperor Shun?

sentences.zh: 大學士翟鑾起廢棄中，授以巡邊之寄，乃優遊曼衍，靡費供億。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretary Zhai Luan was raised from the discarded and entrusted with the charge of touring the borders, yet he wandered at leisure in elaborate display, lavishly consuming provisions and funds.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhai Luan was raised from disgrace and entrusted with touring the borders, yet he wandered at leisure in elaborate display, lavishly consuming provisions and funds.

sentences.zh: 以盛苞苴者為才，獻淫樂者為敬，遂使邊軍益瘠，邊備更弛。

translations.literal: Those who gave lavish gifts he deemed talented; those who presented licentious music he deemed reverent—thus border troops grew leaner and border defense slackened the more.
translations.idiomatic: Those who gave lavish gifts he deemed talented; those who presented licentious music he deemed reverent—so border troops grew leaner and border defenses slackened further.

sentences.zh: 行邊若此，將焉用之！

translations.literal: To tour the borders in this fashion—of what use is he!
translations.idiomatic: To tour the borders in this fashion—of what use is he!

sentences.zh: 故不清政本，天下必不治也。

translations.literal: Therefore without clarifying the root of government, the realm will surely fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore without clarifying the root of government, the realm will surely fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 不易本兵，武功必不競也。」

translations.literal: Without changing the head of military affairs, military achievement will surely not be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Without changing the head of military affairs, military achievement will surely not be achieved."

sentences.zh: 疏入，留不下。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was kept and not released.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, it was kept and not acted upon.

sentences.zh: 嵩復疏辯，帝更慰諭，瑜復被譙讓。

translations.literal: Song again memorialized in defense; the Emperor comforted him still more and Yu was again rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Song again memorialized in defense; the Emperor comforted him still more and Yu was rebuked again.

sentences.zh: 然是時帝雖響嵩，猶未深罪言者，嵩亦以初得政，未敢顯擠陷，故瑜得居職如故。

translations.literal: Yet at this time though the Emperor inclined toward Song he had not yet deeply blamed those who spoke; Song too, having just gained power, did not dare openly entrap them, so Yu was able to remain in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at this time, though the Emperor inclined toward Song, he had not yet deeply punished those who spoke out; Song too, having just gained power, did not dare openly entrap them, so Yu remained in office as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，假他事貶其官。

translations.literal: Before long, on a pretext in another matter his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on a pretext in another matter his rank was reduced.

sentences.zh: 又三載，大計，嵩密諷主者黜之。

translations.literal: Three years later, at the great evaluation, Song secretly urged the presiding official to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, at the great evaluation, Song secretly urged the presiding official to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 比疏上，令如貪酷例除名，瑜遂廢棄，終於家。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, the order was to remove his name according to the precedent for the greedy and cruel; Yu was thus cast aside and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial went up, the order was to remove his name under the precedent for the greedy and cruel; Yu was cast aside and ended his life at home.

sentences.zh: 始瑜之為御史也，武定侯郭勛陳時政，極詆大小諸臣不足任，請復遣內侍出鎮守。

translations.literal: When Yu had first been censor, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun presented views on current affairs, extremely denouncing great and small officials as unfit for office and asking that eunuch ambassadors again be sent to garrison and hold command.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu had first been censor, Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun presented views on current affairs, denouncing great and small officials as unfit for office and asking that eunuch ambassadors again be sent to garrison and hold command.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 瑜抗章奏曰：「勛所論諸事，影響恍惚，而復設鎮守，則其本意所註也。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial in opposition saying: "What Xun discussed in various matters was shadowy and vague, yet in restoring garrison commands his underlying intention is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a memorial in opposition: "What Xun discussed in various matters was shadowy and vague, yet in restoring garrison commands his underlying intention is clear.

sentences.zh: 勛交通內侍，代之營求，利他日重賄。

translations.literal: Xun maintains relations with inner eunuchs, acting on their behalf in pursuit of office, looking to heavy bribes on another day.
translations.idiomatic: Xun maintains relations with inner eunuchs, acting on their behalf in pursuit of office, looking to heavy bribes on another day.

sentences.zh: 其言：『官吏貪濁，由陛下無心腹耳目之人在四方』。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Officials are greedy and corrupt because Your Majesty has no trusted eyes and ears in the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Officials are greedy and corrupt because Your Majesty has no trusted eyes and ears in the four quarters.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：『文武懷奸避事，許內臣劾奏，則奸貪自息』。

translations.literal: And he said: 'When civil and military officials harbor treachery and shirk affairs, permit inner eunuchs to impeach them, and treacherous corruption will of itself cease.'
translations.idiomatic: And he said: 'When civil and military officials harbor treachery and shirk affairs, permit inner eunuchs to impeach them, and treacherous corruption will cease of itself.'

sentences.zh: 果若勛言，則內臣用事莫如正德時，其為太平極治耶？

translations.literal: If Xun's words were true, then never were inner eunuchs so powerful as under the Zhengde reign—was that an age of extreme peace and perfect governance?
translations.idiomatic: If Xun's words were true, then never were inner eunuchs so powerful as under the Zhengde reign—was that an age of supreme peace and perfect governance?

sentences.zh: 陛下革鎮守內臣，誠聖明善政，而勛詆以偏私。

translations.literal: Your Majesty abolished garrison eunuchs—a truly sage and brilliant policy—yet Xun slandered it as partial favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty abolished garrison eunuchs—a truly sage and enlightened policy—yet Xun slandered it as partial favoritism.

sentences.zh: 在朝百官，孰非天子耳目？

translations.literal: Of the hundred officials at court, who is not the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears?
translations.idiomatic: Of the hundred officials at court, who is not the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears?

sentences.zh: 而勛詆以不足任。

translations.literal: Yet Xun slandered them as unfit to bear office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xun slandered them as unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 欲陛下盡疑天下士大夫，獨倚宦官為腹心耳目，臣不知勛視陛下為何如主？」

translations.literal: He wishes Your Majesty wholly to distrust the scholar-officials of the realm and rely on eunuchs alone as trusted eyes and ears—your servant does not know what sort of sovereign Xun takes Your Majesty to be?
translations.idiomatic: He wishes Your Majesty wholly to distrust the scholar-officials of the realm and rely on eunuchs alone as trusted eyes and ears—I do not know what sort of sovereign Xun takes Your Majesty to be?

sentences.zh: 會給事中朱隆禧亦以為言，勛奏始寢。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Zhu Longxi also spoke to this effect, and Xun's memorial was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhu Longxi also spoke to this effect, and Xun's memorial was then shelved.

sentences.zh: 瑜，隆慶初復官贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Yu, at the beginning of Longqing, had his office restored and was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, at the beginning of the Longqing reign, had his office restored and was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 王曄，字韜孟，金壇人。

translations.literal: Wang Ye, style Taomeng, was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ye, styled Taomeng, came from Jintan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授吉安推官，召拜南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Ji'an, he was summoned and appointed supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Ji'an, he was summoned and appointed supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月偕同官上言：「外寇陸梁，本兵張瓚及總督尚書樊繼祖、新遷侍郎費寀不堪重寄」。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twentieth year, together with his colleagues he memorialized: "Outer bandits run riot; the head of military affairs Zhang Zan and the supervising minister Fan Jizu and the newly transferred Vice Minister Fei Cai are unfit to bear heavy trust."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twentieth year he and his colleagues memorialized: "Outer bandits run riot; head of military affairs Zhang Zan, supervising minister Fan Jizu, and newly transferred Vice Minister Fei Cai are unfit to bear heavy trust."

sentences.zh: 帝下其章於所司。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent their memorial to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor referred their memorial to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 居兩月，復劾瓚，因及禮部尚書嚴嵩、總督侍郎胡守中，與巨奸郭勛相結納。

translations.literal: Two months later, they again impeached Zan, and furthermore the Minister of Rites Yan Song, the supervising Vice Minister Hu Shouzhong, and their collusion with the great villain Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later they again impeached Zan, and also Minister of Rites Yan Song, supervising Vice Minister Hu Shouzhong, and their collusion with the great villain Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 嵩所居第宅，則勛私人代營之。

translations.literal: The residence in which Song lived was built for him by men in Xun's private employ.
translations.idiomatic: The mansion in which Yan Song lived had been built for him by Guo Xun's private agents.

sentences.zh: 逾月，御史伊敏生、鄭蕓、陳策亦雲嵩居宅乃勛私人孫澐所居，澐籍沒，嵩第應在籍中。

translations.literal: After a month, the censors Yi Minsheng, Zheng Yun, and Chen Ce also said that Song's dwelling was the residence formerly occupied by Sun Yun, a man in Xun's private employ; Yun's property had been confiscated, and Song's mansion ought to be on the forfeited register.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, censors Yi Minsheng, Zheng Yun, and Chen Ce likewise reported that Yan Song's residence was the house formerly occupied by Sun Yun, a retainer of Guo Xun; since Yun's property had been confiscated, Song's mansion should have been included in the forfeited estate.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪敏生等俸一級。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and reduced Minsheng and the others' salaries by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and stripped one rank of salary from Minsheng and the others.

sentences.zh: 嵩不問，而守中竟由曄疏獲罪。

translations.literal: Song was not questioned, but Shouzhong in the end was punished because of Ye's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song went unprosecuted, yet Hu Shouzhong was ultimately punished on account of Wang Ye's memorial.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，嵩入內閣。

translations.literal: The next autumn, Song entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn, Yan Song entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中沈良才、御史喻時等交章劾嵩。

translations.literal: The chief supervising secretary of the Secretariat of the Ministry of Personnel, Shen Liangcai, the censor Yu Shi, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Song.
translations.idiomatic: Chief supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Personnel Shen Liangcai, censor Yu Shi, and others submitted a stream of memorials impeaching Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 逾月，山西巡按童漢臣章上。

translations.literal: After a month, the memorial of the Shanxi surveillance commissioner Tong Hanchen arrived.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, the memorial of Shanxi surveillance commissioner Tong Hanchen reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 又逾月，曄與同官陳塏、御史陳紹等章亦上。

translations.literal: After yet another month, memorials from Ye together with his colleague Chen Kan and the censor Chen Shao and others also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Another month later, memorials from Wang Ye, his colleague Chen Kan, censor Chen Shao, and others also arrived.

sentences.zh: 大指皆論嵩奸貪，而曄疏並及嵩子世蕃，語尤剴切，帝皆不省。

translations.literal: Their main thrust everywhere discussed Song's treachery and greed; Ye's memorial also reached Song's son Shifan, and the language was especially incisive, yet the Emperor took notice of none of it.
translations.idiomatic: All alike charged Yan Song with treachery and greed; Ye's memorial also named Song's son Shifan, and its language was especially cutting, yet the Emperor paid no heed to any of them.

sentences.zh: 嵩憾甚，未有以中也。

translations.literal: Song harbored deep resentment but had no means yet to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song nursed a deep grudge but as yet had no way to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 久之，為山東僉事，給由入都，道病後期，嵩遂奪其官。

translations.literal: After a long time, he became an assistant commissioner in Shandong; traveling to the capital with his credentials, he fell ill on the road and arrived late, and Song thereupon stripped him of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was appointed assistant commissioner in Shandong; while proceeding to the capital with his credentials he fell ill en route and arrived late, whereupon Yan Song stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 曄在臺，嘗劾罷方面官三十九人，直聲甚著。

translations.literal: When Ye was at the Censorate, he had once impeached and removed thirty-nine regional officials, and his reputation for uprightness was very notable.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Ye served at the Censorate he had once impeached and removed thirty-nine regional officials, and his reputation for moral courage was widely known.

sentences.zh: 比歸，環堵蕭然，數年卒。

translations.literal: When he returned home, his bare walls were utterly desolate; he died several years later.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home his dwelling was bare and destitute; he died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 伊敏生，上元人。

translations.literal: Yi Minsheng was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Minsheng came from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 鄭蕓、陳策，俱莆田人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yun and Chen Ce were both natives of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yun and Chen Ce were both from Putian.

sentences.zh: 敏生官至山東參政。

translations.literal: Minsheng rose in office to administrative commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Minsheng rose to become administrative commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 策，臺州知府。

translations.literal: Ce ended as prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ce ended his career as prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 蕓，終御史。

translations.literal: Yun ended as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yun ended his career as a censor.

sentences.zh: 沈良才，泰州人。

translations.literal: Shen Liangcai was a native of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Liangcai came from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 起家庶吉士，歷官至兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose from a Hanlin bachelor and rose through offices to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Hanlin bachelor and rose through the ranks to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三十六年大計自陳，已調南京矣，嵩附批南京科道拾遺疏中，落其職。

translations.literal: In the great triennial evaluation of the thirty-sixth year he submitted a self-report; he had already been transferred to Nanjing, yet Song attached a note to the Nanjing censorate's memorial on omissions and had him dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the triennial evaluation of the thirty-sixth year he filed a self-report; though already transferred to Nanjing, Yan Song appended a note to the Nanjing censorate's memorial on official omissions and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 喻時，光山人。

translations.literal: Yu Shi was a native of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shi came from Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 官至南京兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose in office to Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 童漢臣，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Tong Hanchen was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Hanchen came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 由魏縣知縣入為御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Wei County he entered service as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced from magistrate of Wei County to censor.

sentences.zh: 寇大入宣府、大同，總督樊繼祖等掩敗，三以捷聞。

translations.literal: When bandits made a major incursion into Xuanda and Datong, the grand coordinator Fan Jizu and others concealed defeat and three times reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders made a major incursion into Xuanda and Datong, grand coordinator Fan Jizu and others concealed their defeats and three times reported victories.

sentences.zh: 漢臣等劾之，得罪。

translations.literal: Hanchen and others impeached them and were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchen and others impeached them and themselves were punished.

sentences.zh: 其按山西，督諸將擊卻俺答之薄太原者，會方劾嵩，觸其怒。

translations.literal: When he inspected Shanxi, he directed the generals to repel Altan's forces pressing Taiyuan; it happened that he was then impeaching Song and touched his anger.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Shanxi he directed the generals to repel Altan's forces as they pressed Taiyuan; he was at the same time impeaching Yan Song, which provoked Song's wrath.

sentences.zh: 明年，漢臣與巡撫李玨覈上繼祖等失事狀。

translations.literal: The next year, Hanchen together with the grand coordinator Li Jue jointly verified and memorialized the record of Jizu and the others' failures.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Hanchen and grand coordinator Li Jue jointly verified and memorialized the failures of Fan Jizu and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 章下吏部。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 漢臣前劾嵩並劾吏部尚書許贊，贊亦憾漢臣。

translations.literal: Hanchen had earlier impeached Song and also impeached the Minister of Personnel Xu Zan; Zan likewise resented Hanchen.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchen had earlier impeached Yan Song and also impeached Minister of Personnel Xu Zan, who likewise bore a grudge against Hanchen.

sentences.zh: 因言漢臣劾遲延，宜並論。

translations.literal: He therefore said that Hanchen's impeachment had been delayed and that both matters ought to be discussed together.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore argued that Hanchen's impeachment had been unduly delayed and that both charges should be adjudicated together.

sentences.zh: 嵩遂擬旨鐫玨一階留任，謫漢臣湖廣布政司都事。

translations.literal: Song then drafted the rescript reducing Jue by one rank while retaining him in office, and demoting Hanchen to director-general of affairs in the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song then drafted the rescript reducing Li Jue by one rank while keeping him in post, and demoting Hanchen to director-general of affairs in the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 舉朝皆知為嵩所中，莫能救也。

translations.literal: The whole court knew that he had been struck down by Song, yet none could save him.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court knew Hanchen had been brought down by Yan Song, yet no one could save him.

sentences.zh: 久之，為泉州知府。

translations.literal: After a long time, he became prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was appointed prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 倭賊薄城，有保障功。

translations.literal: When pirate raiders pressed the city, he had merit in its defense.
translations.idiomatic: When pirate raiders pressed the city, he earned merit in its defense.

sentences.zh: 終江西副使。

translations.literal: He ended as vice commissioner in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice commissioner in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 陳塏，余姚人。

translations.literal: Chen Kan was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kan came from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 後為嵩斥罷。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed by Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed by Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 何維柏，字喬仲，南海人。

translations.literal: He Weibai, style Qiaozhong, was a native of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He Weibai, styled Qiaozhong, came from Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授御史。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 雷震謹身殿，維柏言四海困竭，所在流移，而所司議加賦，民不為盜不止。

translations.literal: When thunder shook the Jinshen Hall, Weibai said that the four seas were exhausted, people were displaced everywhere, yet the responsible offices discussed raising taxes—unless the people became bandits, it would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder shook the Jinshen Hall, Weibai said the empire was exhausted, displacement was everywhere, yet the responsible offices still discussed raising taxes; unless the people turned to banditry, the disorder would not cease.

sentences.zh: 因請罷沙河行宮、金山功德寺工作，及安南問罪之師。

translations.literal: He therefore asked to halt work on the Shahe traveling palace and the Jinshan Merit Temple, and the punitive expedition against Annan.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked to halt construction of the Shahe traveling palace and the Jinshan Merit Temple, and the punitive campaign against Annan.

sentences.zh: 帝頗嘉納。

translations.literal: The Emperor rather praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor largely approved and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起巡按福建。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was recalled as surveillance commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled to serve as surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十四年五月疏劾大學士嚴嵩奸貪罪，比之李林甫、盧杞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year he memorialized impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song for treacherous and greedy crimes, comparing him to Li Linfu and Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year he memorialized impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song for treachery and greed, comparing him to Li Linfu and Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 且言嵩進顧可學、盛端明修合方藥，邪媚要寵。

translations.literal: He also said that Song had advanced Gu Kexue and Sheng Duanming to prepare elixir formulas, wicked flattery to court favor.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Song had promoted Gu Kexue and Sheng Duanming to prepare elixir prescriptions, using wicked flattery to win imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，遣官逮治。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and sent officials to arrest and try him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly enraged and sent officials to arrest and try him.

sentences.zh: 士民遮道號哭，維柏意氣自如。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners blocked the road weeping; Weibai's spirit remained as composed as ever.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners blocked the road in tears, yet Weibai's bearing remained as composed as ever.

sentences.zh: 下詔獄，廷杖，除名。

translations.literal: He was sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and his name was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 家居二十余年。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 隆慶改元，召復官，擢大理少卿。

translations.literal: When the Longqing reign began, he was summoned to restore his office and was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was summoned back to office and promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 遷左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏請日禦便殿，召執政大臣謀政事，並擇大臣有才德者與講讀儒臣更番入直。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting daily attendance at the convenient hall, summoning the chief ministers to deliberate on government affairs, and also selecting talented and virtuous ministers to rotate in attendance with the Confucian lecturers on duty.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that the Emperor hold daily audience in the convenient hall, summon the chief ministers to deliberate on state affairs, and select talented and virtuous ministers to rotate in attendance with the Confucian lecturers on duty.

sentences.zh: 宮中燕居，慎選謹厚內侍調護聖躬，俾遊處有常，幸禦有節。

translations.literal: When at leisure within the palace, carefully choose prudent and solid inner attendants to tend the imperial person, so that recreation has regularity and imperial visits have restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In palace leisure he urged careful selection of prudent, solid eunuchs to attend the imperial person, so that recreation had fixed limits and imperial outings were restrained.

sentences.zh: 非隆冬盛寒，毋輟朝講。

translations.literal: Unless in deep winter or severe cold, do not cease court lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Except in deep winter or bitter cold, court lectures should not be suspended.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: Word came back acknowledging the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged his memorial.

sentences.zh: 進左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his mother's death he returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，還朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wanli reign he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wanli reign he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左、右侍郎，極論鬻官之害。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel and vigorously discussed the harm of selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel and spoke at length on the evils of selling offices.

sentences.zh: 御史劉臺劾大學士張居正，居正乞罷，維柏倡九卿留之。

translations.literal: When the censor Liu Tai impeached Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and Juzheng begged to resign, Weibai led the nine ministers in urging that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Liu Tai impeached Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and Juzheng asked to resign, Weibai led the nine ministers in urging that he remain in office.

sentences.zh: 及居正遭父喪，詔吏部諭留。

translations.literal: When Juzheng encountered his father's mourning, an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to instruct him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng entered mourning for his father, an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to instruct him to remain at his post.

sentences.zh: 尚書張瀚叩維柏，維柏曰：「天經地義，何可廢也？」

translations.literal: The Minister Zhang Han asked Weibai; Weibai said: "Heaven's constant and earth's righteousness—how can they be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Han consulted Weibai; Weibai replied, "Heaven's constant and earth's righteousness—how can they be set aside?

sentences.zh: 瀚從之而止。

translations.literal: Han followed him and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han followed his counsel and desisted.

sentences.zh: 居正怒，取旨罷瀚，停維柏俸三月。

translations.literal: Juzheng was angry, took a rescript to dismiss Han, and suspended Weibai's salary for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was enraged, obtained a rescript dismissing Zhang Han, and suspended Weibai's salary for three months.

sentences.zh: 旋出為南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was sent out as Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 考察自陳，居正從中罷之。

translations.literal: In the evaluation he submitted a self-report; Juzheng had him dismissed from within.
translations.idiomatic: In the triennial evaluation he filed a self-report; Juzheng had him dismissed from behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 卒謚端恪。

translations.literal: When he died he was given the posthumous title Duangong.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was given the posthumous title Duangong.

sentences.zh: 徐學詩，字以言，上虞人。

translations.literal: Xu Xueshi, style Yiyan, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xueshi, styled Yiyan, came from Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice and rose to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice and rose to department director.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，俺答薄京師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Altan pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Altan pressed the capital.

sentences.zh: 既退，詔廷臣陳制敵之策。

translations.literal: After the enemy withdrew, an edict ordered the court ministers to present policies for controlling the foe.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, an edict ordered court ministers to present policies for dealing with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 諸臣多掇細事以應。

translations.literal: Many ministers picked up minor matters to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers offered only petty measures in reply.

sentences.zh: 學詩憤然曰：「大奸柄國，亂之本也。

translations.literal: Xueshi said angrily: "A great villain holds the state—the root of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xueshi said in anger, "A great villain holds the state—that is the root of disorder.

sentences.zh: 亂本不除，能攘外患哉？」

translations.literal: If the root of disorder is not removed, can outer calamity be repelled?
translations.idiomatic: If the root of disorder is not removed, how can outer threats be repelled?

sentences.zh: 即上疏言：

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 大學士嵩輔政十載，奸貪異甚。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Song has aided government for ten years; treachery and greed are extremely great.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yan Song has directed government for ten years; his treachery and greed are extreme.

sentences.zh: 內結權貴，外比群小。

translations.literal: Inwardly he bonds with the powerful and noble; outwardly he bands with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly he bonds with the powerful and noble; outwardly he bands with petty men.

sentences.zh: 文武遷除，率邀厚賄，致此輩掊克軍民，釀成寇患。

translations.literal: Civil and military appointments and dismissals mostly invite heavy bribes, causing these men to extort military and civilians and brew border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military appointments and dismissals are mostly bought with heavy bribes, driving his followers to squeeze the army and the people and breed border troubles.

sentences.zh: 國事至此，猶敢謬引佳兵不祥之說，以謾清問。

translations.literal: State affairs have come to this point, yet he still dares wrongly to cite the saying that excellent troops are inauspicious, to deceive the imperial inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: With state affairs at such a pass, he still dares wrongly to cite the saying that fine weapons are inauspicious, so as to deceive the Emperor's inquiry.

sentences.zh: 近因都城有警，密輸財賄南還。

translations.literal: Recently, because the capital had an alarm, he secretly transported wealth and bribes south.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the capital was threatened, he secretly shipped wealth and bribes south.

sentences.zh: 大車數十乘，樓船十余艘，水陸載道，駭人耳目。

translations.literal: Several dozen large carts and more than ten tower boats filled the roads by land and water, shocking eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen large carts and more than ten tower ships filled the roads by land and water, shocking all who saw them.

sentences.zh: 又納奪職總兵官李鳳鳴二千金，使鎮薊州，受老廢總兵官郭琮三千金，使督漕運。

translations.literal: He also accepted two thousand taels from the stripped regional commander Li Fengming to let him garrison Jizhou, and three thousand taels from the old dismissed regional commander Guo Cong to let him supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He also took two thousand taels from Li Fengming, a regional commander stripped of office, to let him garrison Jizhou, and three thousand taels from Guo Cong, an old dismissed regional commander, to let him supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 諸如此比，難可悉數。

translations.literal: Cases like these are hard to enumerate fully.
translations.idiomatic: Cases like these are too numerous to recount in full.

sentences.zh: 舉朝莫不嘆憤，而無有一人敢牴牾者，誠以內外盤結，上下比周，積久勢成。

translations.literal: The whole court none but sighed in anger, yet not one person dared to oppose him—truly because inner and outer were entwined, upper and lower banded together, and long accumulation had formed its force.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court seethed with indignation, yet not one man dared openly to defy him—truly because court and provinces were entangled, superiors and subordinates colluded, and long accumulation had made his power unassailable.

sentences.zh: 而其子世蕃又兇狡成性，擅執父權。

translations.literal: Moreover his son Shifan is fierce and cunning by nature and usurps his father's power.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his son Shifan is fierce and cunning by nature and usurps his father's authority.

sentences.zh: 凡諸司奏請，必先白其父子，然後敢聞於陛下。

translations.literal: Whatever office memorials request, they must first be reported to father and son, and only then dare they be brought before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever memorial any office submits must first be cleared with father and son before it dare reach Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦安得而盡悉之乎？

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty fully know all of it?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty fully know any of it?

sentences.zh: 蓋嵩權力足以假手下石，機械足以先發制人，勢利足以廣交自固，文詞便給足以掩罪飾非。

translations.literal: For Song's power is sufficient to borrow others' hands to cast stones; his machinations are sufficient to strike first and control others; his influence is sufficient to widen alliances and secure himself; his fluent prose is sufficient to cover crimes and gloss over wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song's power is enough to use others' hands to strike down his foes; his schemes are enough to strike first and control others; his influence is enough to weave alliances and entrench himself; his glib prose is enough to cover crimes and gloss over wrongs.

sentences.zh: 而精悍警敏，揣摩巧中，足以趨利避害；

translations.literal: And his keen alertness and agility are sufficient to pursue benefit and avoid harm.
translations.idiomatic: His sharp vigilance and agility are enough to seize advantage and evade harm.

sentences.zh: 彌縫缺失，私交密惠，令色脂言，又足以結人歡心，箝人口舌。

translations.literal: Patching over gaps, private exchanges and secret favors, pleasing looks and oily words are also sufficient to win people's hearts and clamp their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Papering over faults, private deals and secret favors, pleasing looks and oily speech are also enough to win men's hearts and silence their tongues.

sentences.zh: 故前後論嵩者，嵩雖不能顯禍之於正言之時，莫不假事托人陰中之於遷除考察之際。

translations.literal: Therefore those who before and after criticized Song—though Song could not openly harm them at the time of upright speech—none failed to use borrowed affairs and people to strike at them secretly at the junctures of transfer and evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those who criticized Yan Song before and after—though he could not openly ruin them when they spoke plainly—none failed to be struck down secretly through contrived charges at the moments of transfer and triennial evaluation.

sentences.zh: 如前給事中王曄、陳塏，御史謝瑜、童漢臣輩，於時亦蒙寬宥，而今皆安在哉？

translations.literal: Such as the former supervising secretary Wang Ye and Chen Kan, the censors Xie Yu and Tong Hanchen and the like—at the time they also received lenient pardon; where are they now?
translations.idiomatic: Such as the former supervising secretaries Wang Ye and Chen Kan, censors Xie Yu and Tong Hanchen, and the like—at the time they too were spared; where are they now?

sentences.zh: 陛下誠罷嵩父子，別簡忠良代之，外患自無不寧矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly dismisses the Song father and son and separately selects the loyal and good to replace them, outer troubles naturally will not fail to be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly dismisses the Song father and son and separately appoints loyal and capable men in their place, outer troubles will naturally be pacified.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，頗感動。

translations.literal: The Emperor, reading the memorial, was rather moved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, reading the memorial, was somewhat moved.

sentences.zh: 方士陶仲文密言嵩孤立盡忠，學詩特為所私修隙耳。

translations.literal: The Daoist adept Tao Zhongwen secretly said that Song was isolated and utterly loyal, and that Xueshi had specially nursed a private grudge and manufactured a quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist adept Tao Zhongwen secretly told the Emperor that Yan Song stood alone in utter loyalty, and that Xu Xueshi had merely nursed a private grudge and manufactured a quarrel.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發怒，下之詔獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon grew angry and sent him to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon flew into a rage and had him sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 嵩不自安，求去，帝優詔慰諭。

translations.literal: Yan Song was ill at ease and asked to leave; the Emperor with a gracious edict comforted and reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song, ill at ease, asked to resign; the Emperor issued a gracious edict to comfort and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 嵩疏謝，佯為世蕃乞回籍，帝亦不許。

translations.literal: Song submitted a memorial of thanks, feigning to beg that Yan Shifan return to his native place; the Emperor also did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song submitted a memorial of thanks, feigning to ask that Yan Shifan be allowed to retire to his native place; the Emperor would not allow that either.

sentences.zh: 學詩竟削籍。

translations.literal: Xu Xueshi in the end was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xueshi was in the end struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 先劾嵩者葉經、謝瑜、陳紹與學詩皆同里，時稱「上虞四諫」。

translations.literal: Those who had earlier impeached Song—Ye Jing, Xie Yu, and Chen Shao—were all fellow townsmen with Xueshi; at the time they were called the "Four Remonstrators of Shangyu."
translations.idiomatic: Those who had first impeached Yan Song—Ye Jing, Xie Yu, and Chen Shao—were all from the same district as Xu Xueshi; contemporaries called them the "Four Remonstrators of Shangyu."

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，起學詩南京通政參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, Xu Xueshi was recalled as vice director of the Nanjing Transmission Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign Xu Xueshi was recalled as vice director of the Nanjing Transmission Office.

sentences.zh: 未之官，卒。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he died.

sentences.zh: 贈大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Vice Minister of the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 初，學詩族兄應豐以善書擢中書舍人，供事無逸殿，悉嵩所為。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xueshi's clansman elder brother Yingfeng, for skill in calligraphy, was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, serving in the Hall of Unceasing Ease; all was Yan Song's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Xueshi's elder clansman Yingfeng had been promoted to Secretariat Drafter for his skill in calligraphy and served in the Hall of Unceasing Ease—all through Yan Song's patronage.

sentences.zh: 嵩疑學詩疏出應豐指，會考察，屬吏部斥之。

translations.literal: Song suspected Xueshi's memorial came from Yingfeng's prompting; when the evaluation came, he had the Ministry of Personnel dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song suspected Xu Xueshi's memorial had been prompted by Yingfeng; when the triennial evaluation came, he had the Ministry of Personnel dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 應豐詣迎和門辭，特旨留用，嵩恚益甚。

translations.literal: Yingfeng went to the Yinghe Gate to take leave; by special edict he was kept in post, and Song's rage grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yingfeng went to the Yinghe Gate to bid farewell; a special edict kept him in office, and Yan Song's rage grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 居數年以誤寫科書譖於帝，竟杖殺之。

translations.literal: After several years in office, for a mistaken transcription in a rostered document he slandered him to the Emperor, and in the end had him beaten to death at court.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, for a mistaken transcription in a roster document he slandered him to the Emperor and in the end had him beaten to death at court.

sentences.zh: 陳紹終韶州知府。

translations.literal: Chen Shao ended as prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shao ended his career as prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 厲汝進，字子修，灤州人。

translations.literal: Li Rujin, style Zixiu, was a native of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rujin, style Zixiu, was a native of Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eleventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授池州推官，征拜吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Chizhou and was summoned to be supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Chizhou, then summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 湖廣巡撫陸傑以顯陵工成，召為工部等郎。

translations.literal: The Huguang grand coordinator Lu Jie, because the Xian Mausoleum works were completed, was recalled as a director and the like in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jie, grand coordinator of Huguang, was recalled to the Ministry of Works as a director and the like once the Xian Mausoleum works were completed.

sentences.zh: 汝進言傑素犯清議，不宜佐司空，並劾尚書甘為霖、樊繼祖不職。

translations.literal: Rujin said Jie had long offended clear opinion and ought not assist the Minister of Works, and together impeached the Ministers Gan Weilin and Fan Jizu for dereliction.
translations.idiomatic: Rujin argued that Jie had long offended public opinion and ought not assist the Minister of Works, and jointly impeached Ministers Gan Weilin and Fan Jizu for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 三遷至戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached chief supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he rose to chief supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書王杲下獄，汝進與同官海寧查秉彜、馬平徐養正、巴縣劉起宗、章丘劉祿合疏言：「兩淮副使張祿遣使入都，廣通結納。

translations.literal: When Minister of Revenue Wang Gao was sent to prison, Rujin and his colleagues—Haining's Zha Bingyi, Maping's Xu Yangzheng, Baxian's Liu Qizong, and Zhangqiu's Liu Lu—submitted a joint memorial saying: "The Vice Commissioner of the Two Huai, Zhang Lu, sent envoys to the capital and widely opened channels of connection and patronage.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Revenue Wang Gao was imprisoned, Rujin and his colleagues Zha Bingyi of Haining, Xu Yangzheng of Maping, Liu Qizong of Baxian, and Liu Lu of Zhangqiu jointly memorialized: "The Vice Commissioner of the Two Huai, Zhang Lu, sent envoys to the capital and widely cultivated connections and patronage.

sentences.zh: 如太常少卿嚴世蕃、府丞胡奎等，皆承賂受囑有證。

translations.literal: Such as the Vice Minister of Rites Yan Shifan, the Assistant Intendant Hu Kui, and others—all received bribes and accepted entreaties, with proof.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Vice Minister of Rites Yan Shifan and Assistant Intendant Hu Kui all took bribes and accepted private entreaties, and there is proof.

sentences.zh: 世蕃竊弄父權，嗜賄張焰。」

translations.literal: Yan Shifan usurped his father's power and was insatiably gluttonous for bribes."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shifan usurped his father's authority and was insatiably gluttonous for bribes.

sentences.zh: 詞連倉場尚書王暐。

translations.literal: The words also implicated Granary Commissioner Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial also implicated Granary Commissioner Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 嵩上疏自理，且求援於中官以激帝怒。

translations.literal: Song submitted a memorial to clear himself and moreover sought aid from the inner eunuchs to stir the Emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song submitted a memorial in his own defense and also sought help from palace eunuchs to inflame the Emperor's wrath.

sentences.zh: 帝責其代杲解釋，命廷杖汝進八十，余六十，並謫雲南、廣西典史。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked them for explaining on Gao's behalf, ordered Rujin beaten eighty strokes at court and the rest sixty, and together banished them to be clerks in Yunnan and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked them for speaking on Wang Gao's behalf, ordered Rujin beaten eighty strokes at court and the others sixty, and banished them all to clerkships in Yunnan and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，嵩復假考察，奪汝進職。

translations.literal: The next year, Song again used the evaluation as a pretext and stripped Rujin of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yan Song again used the triennial evaluation as a pretext and stripped Rujin of his office.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，起故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 未至京，卒。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capital, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the capital, he died.

sentences.zh: 秉彜由黃州推官歷戶科左給事中。

translations.literal: Bingyi, from investigating magistrate of Huangzhou, rose through left supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zha Bingyi rose from investigating magistrate of Huangzhou to left supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 數建白時事。

translations.literal: Several times he offered forthright counsel on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly offered forthright counsel on affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 終順天府尹。

translations.literal: He ended as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 養正以庶吉士歷戶科右給事中。

translations.literal: Yangzheng, from Hanlin Bachelor, passed through right supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yangzheng advanced from Hanlin Bachelor through right supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，官至南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Longqing period, his office reached Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he rose to Minister of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 起宗初除衢州推官。

translations.literal: Qizong at first was appointed investigating magistrate of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qizong was first appointed investigating magistrate of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 延綏幾饑，請帑金振救。

translations.literal: Yan-sui was nearly in famine; he requested treasury silver for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan-sui was on the verge of famine, he requested treasury funds for relief.

sentences.zh: 終遼東苑馬寺卿。

translations.literal: He ended as director of the Liaodong Stud Farms.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as director of the Liaodong Stud Farms.

sentences.zh: 祿以行人司擢戶科給事。

translations.literal: Liu, from the Messenger Office, was promoted to supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lu was promoted from the Messenger Office to supervising secretary in the Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 謫後，自免歸。

translations.literal: After banishment, he resigned on his own and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After his banishment he resigned of his own accord and returned home.

sentences.zh: 王宗茂，字時育，京山人。

translations.literal: Wang Zongmao, style Shiyu, was a native of Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongmao, style Shiyu, was a native of Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 父橋，廣東布政使。

translations.literal: His father Qiao was Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiao had served as Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 從父格，太仆卿。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother Ge was Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Ge had served as Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 宗茂登嘉靖二十六年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Zongmao passed the jinshi of the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing and was appointed Messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmao passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing and was appointed Messenger.

sentences.zh: 三十一年擢南京御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to Nanjing Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時先後劾嚴嵩者皆得禍，沈煉至謫佃保安。

translations.literal: At the time those who before and after impeached Yan Song all met disaster; Shen Lian was even banished to tenant-farming at Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: At that time everyone who impeached Yan Song, sooner or later, met disaster; Shen Lian was even banished to farm as a tenant at Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 中外懾其威，益箝口。

translations.literal: Within and without the court they feared his might and clamped their mouths still tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court men feared his power and clamped their mouths tighter still.

sentences.zh: 宗茂積不平，甫拜官三月，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zongmao nursed long indignation; scarcely three months after taking office he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zongmao had long nursed indignation; scarcely three months after taking office he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 嵩本邪諂之徒，寡廉鮮恥。

translations.literal: Song was originally a fawning, sycophantic sort, scant in integrity and thin in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song is by nature a sycophant, scant in integrity and thin in shame.

sentences.zh: 久持國柄，作福作威。

translations.literal: Long holding the state's handle, he plays the lord of blessing and the lord of wrath.
translations.idiomatic: He has long held the reins of state, wielding blessings and terrors as he pleases.

sentences.zh: 薄海內外，罔不怨恨。

translations.literal: Near and far across the seas, none fail to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: From every corner of the realm within the seas, none fail to resent him.

sentences.zh: 如吏、兵二部每選，請屬二十人，人索賄數百金，任自擇善地。

translations.literal: For example, at each selection by the Ministries of Personnel and War he requests twenty men on his behalf; each man is charged a bribe of several hundred taels of silver and may himself choose a good post.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Ministries of Personnel and War make selections, he requests twenty appointments on his behalf; each man pays a bribe of several hundred taels and may choose his own desirable post.

sentences.zh: 致文武將吏盡出其門。

translations.literal: Thus civil and military officers and generals all issue from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus civil officials, military officers, and generals all issue from his gate.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪一也。

translations.literal: This is the first crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's first crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 任私人萬寀為考功郎。

translations.literal: He appointed his private man Wan Cai as Director of Merits.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his private creature Wan Cai as Director of Merits.

sentences.zh: 凡外官遷擢，不察其行能，不計其資歷，唯賄是問。

translations.literal: Whenever an outer official was transferred or promoted, he did not examine conduct and ability, did not reckon seniority—only bribes were asked.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an outside official was transferred or promoted, conduct and ability went unexamined and seniority uncounted—only bribes mattered.

sentences.zh: 致端方之士不得為國家用。

translations.literal: Thus upright men could not be employed for the state's use.
translations.idiomatic: Thus upright men could not be put to the state's service.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪二也。

translations.literal: This is the second crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's second crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 往歲遭人論劾，潛輸家資南返，輦載珍寶，不可數計。

translations.literal: In past years, when others impeached him, he secretly sent his household wealth south; carts loaded with treasures were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In past years, when men impeached him, he secretly shipped his household wealth south; cartloads of treasure were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 金銀人物，多高二三尺者。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, and human figures—many were as tall as two or three chi.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, and human figures—many stood two or three chi high.

sentences.zh: 下至溺器，亦金銀為之。

translations.literal: Down to chamber pots, these too were made of gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Even down to chamber pots, these too were made of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 不知陛下宮中亦有此器否耶？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty's palace also have such vessels, or not?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty's palace also possess such vessels?

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪三也。

translations.literal: This is the third crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's third crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 廣布良田，遍於江西數郡。

translations.literal: He broadly planted fertile fields, spread across several commanderies of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He has planted fertile fields across several commanderies of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 又於府第之後積石為大坎，實以金銀珍玩，為子孫百世計。

translations.literal: Again behind his mansion he piled stone into a great pit and filled it with gold, silver, and precious curios, planning for his descendants for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Behind his mansion he piled stone into a great vault and filled it with gold, silver, and precious curios, laying up wealth for his descendants for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 而國計民瘼，一不措懷。

translations.literal: Yet state accounts and the people's suffering he set his mind to not at all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet state accounts and the people's suffering he does not heed in the least.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's fourth crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 畜家奴五百余人，往來京邸。

translations.literal: He kept more than five hundred household slaves, coming and going at the capital lodges.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps more than five hundred household slaves, coming and going through the capital lodges.

sentences.zh: 所至騷擾驛傳，虐害居民，長吏皆怨怒而不敢言。

translations.literal: Wherever they arrived they harassed relay stations and abused residents; senior officials all resented and raged yet dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they went they harassed relay stations and abused residents; local officials all seethed with anger yet dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's fifth crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下所食大官之饌不數品，而嵩則窮極珍錯。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty eats from the Grand Steward's kitchen is not several kinds, yet Song exhausts every rare delicacy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's table from the Grand Steward's kitchen numbers scarcely a few dishes, yet Yan Song exhausts every rare delicacy.

sentences.zh: 殊方異產，莫不畢致。

translations.literal: Exotic products from distant regions—none fail to be fully gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic products from distant regions—none fail to reach his table.

sentences.zh: 是九州萬國之待嵩有甚於陛下。

translations.literal: Thus the nine regions and ten thousand states wait on Song more than on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the nine regions and ten thousand states serve Yan Song more lavishly than they serve Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's sixth crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 往歲寇迫京畿，正上下憂懼之日，而嵩貪肆益甚。

translations.literal: In past years when bandits pressed on the capital region, it was just the day when above and below were anxious and fearful, yet Song's greed and license grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: When in past years raiders pressed on the capital region—just when court and country were gripped by fear—Yan Song's greed and license grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 致民俗歌謠，遍於京師，達於沙漠。

translations.literal: Thus folk songs and ballads spread through the capital and reached the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Folk songs and ballads spread through the capital and reached the desert.

sentences.zh: 海內百姓，莫不祝天以冀其早亡，嵩尚恬不知止。

translations.literal: The people within the seas—none fail to pray Heaven hoping for his early death—yet Song is still complacent and knows no stop.
translations.idiomatic: The people within the seas all pray Heaven for his early death, yet Yan Song remains complacent and knows no limit.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's seventh crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 募朝士為幹兒義子至三十余輩。

translations.literal: He recruited court gentlemen as sworn sons and godsons to more than thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited more than thirty court gentlemen as sworn sons and godsons.

sentences.zh: 若尹耕、梁紹儒，早已敗露。

translations.literal: Such as Yin Geng and Liang Shaoru had long since been exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Yin Geng and Liang Shaoru had long since been exposed.

sentences.zh: 此輩實衣冠之盜，而皆為之爪牙，助其虐焰，致朝廷恩威不出於陛下。

translations.literal: These men are in truth robbers in official dress, yet all serve as his claws and teeth, helping his cruel flame, so that the court's grace and wrath do not issue from Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: These men are robbers in official dress, yet all serve as his claws and teeth, fanning his cruelty, so that the court's grace and wrath no longer issue from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪八也。

translations.literal: This is the eighth crime by which Song has failed the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yan Song's eighth crime against the state.

sentences.zh: 夫天下之所恃以為安者，財也，兵也。

translations.literal: What the realm relies on for peace is wealth and arms.
translations.idiomatic: What the realm relies on for peace is wealth and arms.

sentences.zh: 不才之文吏，以賂而出其門，則必剝民之財，去百而求千，去千而求萬，民奈何不困？

translations.literal: When incompetent civil clerks leave his gate through bribes, they must strip the people's wealth—taking a hundred they seek a thousand, taking a thousand they seek ten thousand; how can the people not be distressed?
translations.idiomatic: When incompetent civil clerks leave his gate through bribes, they must strip the people—from a hundred they seek a thousand, from a thousand they seek ten thousand; how can the people not be ruined?

sentences.zh: 不才之武將以賂而出其門，則必克軍之餉，或缺伍而不補，或逾期而不發，兵奈何不疲？

translations.literal: When incompetent military officers leave his gate through bribes, they must bite into army rations—sometimes leaving ranks unfilled and not making good the shortfall, sometimes passing the due date and not issuing pay; how can the troops not be worn out?
translations.idiomatic: When incompetent military officers leave his gate through bribes, they must bite into army rations—sometimes leaving ranks unfilled, sometimes missing pay days; how can the troops not be exhausted?

sentences.zh: 邇者，四方地震，其占為臣下專權。

translations.literal: Recently earthquakes in the four quarters—the omen reads as subordinates monopolizing power.
translations.idiomatic: Recently earthquakes have shaken the four quarters—the omen reads as subordinates monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 試問今日之專權者，寧有出於嵩右乎？

translations.literal: Ask: of those who monopolize power today, can any exceed Song?
translations.idiomatic: Ask today who monopolizes power—can any exceed Yan Song?

sentences.zh: 陛下之帑藏不足支諸邊一年之費，而嵩所蓄積可贍儲數年。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's treasury stores are insufficient to supply the border regions for one year, yet what Song has amassed could provision the stores for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's treasury can scarcely supply the borders for one year, yet Yan Song's hoard could fill the stores for several years.

sentences.zh: 與其開賣官鬻爵之令以助邊，盍去此蠹國害民之賊，籍其家以紓患也？

translations.literal: Rather than open orders to sell offices and peddle ranks to aid the borders, why not remove this vermin that harms state and people, register his household property, and ease the distress?
translations.idiomatic: Rather than open orders to sell offices and peddle ranks to aid the borders, why not remove this vermin that harms state and people, confiscate his household property, and ease the distress?

sentences.zh: 臣見數年以來，凡論嵩者不死於廷杖，則役於邊塞。
