translations.literal: Your servant has seen that in recent years, all who criticized Song either died under court beating or were sent to the border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, Your servant has seen, all who criticized Yan Song either died under the court rod or were sent to border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 臣亦有身家，寧不致惜，而敢犯九重之怒，攖權相之鋒哉？

translations.literal: Your servant too has family and person—would he not cherish them?—yet he dares offend the wrath of the Ninefold Brightness and touch the blade of the power-holding minister?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant too has family and life—would he not cherish them?—yet he dares provoke the wrath of the throne and touch the blade of the power-holding minister?

sentences.zh: 誠念世受國恩，不忍見祖宗天下壞於賊嵩之手也。

translations.literal: Truly he thinks he has received the state's grace generation after generation and cannot bear to see the ancestral realm ruined at the hands of the thief Song.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that Your servant has received the state's grace generation after generation and cannot bear to see the ancestral realm ruined by the thief Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 疏至，通政司趙文華密以示嵩，留數日始上，由是嵩得預為地。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Zhao Wenhua of the Transmission Office secretly showed it to Song; it was held several days before being forwarded, and thus Song was able to prepare ground beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Zhao Wenhua of the Transmission Office secretly showed it to Yan Song; it was held several days before being forwarded, and thus Yan Song was able to prepare his ground beforehand.

sentences.zh: 遂以誣詆大臣，謫平陽縣丞。

translations.literal: Thereupon, for slandering and defaming a great minister, he was banished to assistant magistrate of Pingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, on the charge of slandering a great minister, he was banished to assistant magistrate of Pingyang County.

sentences.zh: 方宗茂上疏，自謂必死。

translations.literal: When Zongmao submitted the memorial, he told himself he would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmao submitted his memorial, he was certain he would die.

sentences.zh: 及得貶，恬然出都。

translations.literal: When he received demotion, he calmly left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he was merely demoted, he left the capital calmly.

sentences.zh: 到官半歲，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Half a year after reaching his post, he returned for mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Half a year after taking up his post, he returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 嵩無以釋憾，奪其父橋官。

translations.literal: Song had no way to release his rancor and stripped his father Qiao of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song, unable to vent his rancor, stripped Zongmao's father Qiao of office.

sentences.zh: 橋竟憤悒卒。

translations.literal: Qiao in the end died of indignant distress.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao in the end died of indignant distress.

sentences.zh: 嵩罷相之日，宗茂亦卒。

translations.literal: On the day Song was dismissed from the chancellorship, Zongmao also died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yan Song was dismissed from the chancellorship, Zongmao also died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Directorate for Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longqing reign he was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Director of the Directorate for Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 周冕，資縣人。

translations.literal: Zhou Mian was a man of Zixian County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mian was a native of Zixian County.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授太常博士，擢貴州道試御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was promoted to probationary censor of the Guizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to probationary censor on the Guizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 重建太廟成，奉安神主，帝將遣官代祭。

translations.literal: When reconstruction of the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed and the spirit tablets were installed, the Emperor was about to dispatch officials to perform the sacrifices in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebuilt Imperial Ancestral Temple was finished and the spirit tablets were enshrined, the Emperor intended to send officials to sacrifice in his place.

sentences.zh: 御史鄢懋卿言其不可。

translations.literal: The censor Yan Maoqing said this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Yan Maoqing argued that this should not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，降手詔數百言諭廷臣，且言更有協君取譽者，必罪不宥。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and issued a handwritten edict of several hundred words to instruct the court officials, also saying that anyone else who colluded with the ruler to win praise would certainly be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angry and issued a handwritten edict of several hundred words to admonish the court, adding that anyone else who colluded with the throne for reputation would be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 舉朝悚息，無敢復言，冕獨抗章爭之。

translations.literal: The whole court trembled in fear and none dared speak again; Mian alone submitted a defiant memorial disputing it.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court trembled and none dared speak again, but Mian alone submitted a defiant memorial disputing the policy.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，立下冕詔獄搒掠。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and immediately had Mian thrown into the imperial prison and beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and at once had Mian cast into the imperial prison and flogged.

sentences.zh: 終以其言直，釋還職。

translations.literal: In the end, because his words were straight, he was released and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, because his words were forthright, he was released and restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 是時太子生十一年矣，猶未出閣講學。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent had been born eleven years, yet still had not left the palace to study.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the heir apparent had lived eleven years, yet still had not been brought out of the palace to receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 冕極言教諭不可緩，請早降綸言，慎選侍從。

translations.literal: Mian urgently said that instruction could not be delayed and asked that an edict be issued early and attendants be chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: Mian urgently argued that the heir's education could not be delayed, begging for an early imperial edict and careful selection of attendants.

sentences.zh: 帝又大怒，謫雲南通海縣典史。

translations.literal: The Emperor was again greatly angry and demoted him to clerk of Tonghai County in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged again and demoted him to clerk of Tonghai County in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 冕雖遠竄，意慷慨無所屈。

translations.literal: Though Mian was banished far away, his spirit was generous and unbending.
translations.idiomatic: Though banished far from court, Mian remained generous in spirit and unbowed.

sentences.zh: 數遷至武選郎中。

translations.literal: After several transfers he reached the post of Director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he rose to director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 楊繼盛劾嚴嵩及嚴效忠冒功事，語侵歐陽必進。

translations.literal: Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song and Yan Xiaozhong's false claim of merit, and his language impugned Ouyang Bijin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song and the affair of Yan Xiaozhong's fraudulent merit, and his language also touched Ouyang Bijin.

sentences.zh: 必進奏辯，章下兵部。

translations.literal: Bijin memorialized in his own defense, and the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Bijin memorialized in defense, and the memorial was referred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 冕上言：

translations.literal: Mian memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Mian memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣奉詔檢得二十七年通政司狀，效忠年十六，因武會試未第，咨兩廣軍門聽用。

translations.literal: Your servant, obeying the imperial command, has examined the twenty-seventh-year memorial from the Office of Transmission and found that Xiaozhong was sixteen, and because he had failed the military metropolitan examination, he petitioned the military headquarters of the two Guang provinces for employment.
translations.idiomatic: Obeying Your Majesty's command, your servant has examined the twenty-seventh-year report from the Office of Transmission: Xiaozhong was sixteen, and having failed the military metropolitan examination he petitioned the military headquarters of the two Guang provinces for service.

sentences.zh: 已而必進及總兵官陳圭奏黎賊平，遣效忠報捷，授錦衣試所鎮撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Bijin and the regional commander Chen Gui memorialized that the Li bandits had been pacified and sent Xiaozhong to report victory; he was granted the post of acting battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Bijin and regional commander Chen Gui reported that the Li rebels had been pacified and sent Xiaozhong to announce victory; he was granted the post of acting battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，嚴鵠言兄效忠曾斬首七級，並功加賞，應得署副千戶。

translations.literal: In less than a month Yan Hu said that his elder brother Xiaozhong had once cut off seven heads and that merit should be rewarded together, and he should receive the acting post of vice battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Yan Hu claimed that his elder brother Xiaozhong had once taken seven heads and that the combined merit entitled him to an acting vice battalion commandership.

sentences.zh: 今效忠身抱痼疾，鵠請代職。

translations.literal: Now Xiaozhong is afflicted with a chronic illness, and Hu asks to take his post in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xiaozhong suffers a chronic illness, and Hu asks to hold the post in his place.

sentences.zh: 臣心疑其偽，方將核實以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant suspected fraud and was about to verify the facts and report.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant suspected fraud and was about to verify the facts before reporting.

sentences.zh: 嵩子世蕃乃自創一槁付臣，屬臣依違題覆。

translations.literal: Song's son Shifan then himself composed a draft and gave it to your servant, instructing your servant to reply evasively.
translations.idiomatic: Song's son Shifan then composed a draft himself and handed it to your servant, directing him to answer evasively.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其槁，率誕謾舛戾，請得一一折之。

translations.literal: Your servant examined the draft and found it mostly absurd, reckless, and contradictory, and asks leave to refute it point by point.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant examined the draft and found it for the most part absurd, reckless, and contradictory, and asks leave to refute it point by point.

sentences.zh: 如效忠曾中武舉，何初無本籍起送文牒，今又稱民人，而不言武舉？

translations.literal: If Xiaozhong had once passed the military provincial examination, why at first was there no dispatch document from his native registry, and now he is called a commoner without mention of the military examination?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong had passed the military provincial examination, why was there at first no dispatch document from his native registry, and why is he now called a commoner with no mention of that examination?

sentences.zh: 如效忠果鵠之兄，世蕃之子，則世蕃數子俱幼，未有名效忠者。

translations.literal: If Xiaozhong were truly Hu's elder brother and Shifan's son, then all of Shifan's sons were still young and none was named Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong were truly Hu's elder brother and Shifan's son, then all of Shifan's sons were still young and none bore the name Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 如效忠果斬首七級，則當時狀稱年止十六，豈能赴戰？

translations.literal: If Xiaozhong had truly cut off seven heads, the memorial at the time said he was only sixteen—how could he have gone to battle?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong had truly taken seven heads, the report at the time said he was only sixteen—how could he have gone into battle?

sentences.zh: 何軍門諸將俱未聞斬獲功，獨宰相一孫乃驍勇冠三軍？

translations.literal: Why had none of the generals at the military headquarters heard of merit in cutting heads and capturing enemies, yet the chief minister's grandson alone was said to be the bravest in the three armies?
translations.idiomatic: Why had none of the commanders at headquarters reported such captures, while the chief minister's grandson alone was called the bravest in the three armies?

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠對敵，脛臂受創，計臨陣及差委，相去未一月，何以萬里軍情即能馳報？

translations.literal: If it is said that Xiaozhong faced the enemy and his shins and arms were wounded, considering the time from entering battle to his assignment, less than a month had passed—how could military intelligence ten thousand li away have been reported so swiftly?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong faced the enemy and wounded shins and arms, the time from battle to reassignment was less than a month—how could news from armies ten thousand li away have arrived so fast?

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠到京以創甚疾故，何以鵠代職之日，止告不能受職？

translations.literal: If it is said that Xiaozhong came to the capital because his wounds were grave, why on the day Hu asked to take his post did he report only that he could not accept the office?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong came to the capital because his wounds were grave, why on the day Hu asked to replace him did he report only that he could not take the post?

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠鎮撫當代，則奏捷功止及身，例無傳襲。

translations.literal: If it is said that Xiaozhong's battalion command should be replaced, then the victory report applied only to him personally and by precedent there was no hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong's command should be handed on, the victory report covered only him personally, and by precedent there was no hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠功當並論，例先奏請，何止用通狀，而逼令司官奉行？

translations.literal: If it is said that Xiaozhong's merit should be discussed together, by precedent one should first memorialize and request approval—why use only the transmission office report and force the responsible official to comply?
translations.idiomatic: If his merit should be counted together, precedent required a memorial of request first—why rely only on the transmission report and compel the responsible official to obey?

sentences.zh: 臣悉心廉訪，初未有名效忠者赴軍門聽用，鵠亦非效忠親弟。

translations.literal: Your servant has investigated thoroughly and at first there was no one named Xiaozhong who went to the military headquarters for service, and Hu is not Xiaozhong's younger brother by blood.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has investigated thoroughly: at first no one named Xiaozhong went to headquarters for service, and Hu is not Xiaozhong's true younger brother.

sentences.zh: 其姓名乃詭設，首級亦要買，而非有纖毫實跡也。

translations.literal: The name was a fraudulent invention, the heads were bought, and there was not the slightest trace of truth.
translations.idiomatic: The name was invented, the heads were purchased, and there was not the slightest truth in it.

sentences.zh: 必進既嵩鄉曲，圭又世蕃姻親，依阿朋比，共為欺罔。

translations.literal: Bijin was Song's fellow townsman and Gui was Shifan's relation by marriage; they fawned and banded together in mutual deception.
translations.idiomatic: Bijin was Song's fellow townsman and Gui was related to Shifan by marriage; they fawned on one another and together practiced deceit.

sentences.zh: 臣如不言，陛下何從知其奸？

translations.literal: If your servant did not speak, how would Your Majesty know their treachery?
translations.idiomatic: If your servant did not speak, how would Your Majesty learn of their treachery?

sentences.zh: 且自累朝以來，未聞有宰相之子孫送軍門報效者。

translations.literal: Moreover, since successive dynasties, there has never been heard of a chief minister's son or grandson sent to a military headquarters to report for service.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since antiquity within the dynasty, no chief minister's son or grandson has been sent to a military headquarters to serve.

sentences.zh: 今嵩不唯咨送軍門，而且詭托名姓，破壞祖宗之制，彼蔣應奎、唐國相輩何怪其效尤耶？

translations.literal: Now Song not only petitioned to send him to the military headquarters but also falsely borrowed a name, destroying the institutions of the ancestors—should Jiang Yingkui, Tang Guoxiang, and their kind be blamed for following his example?
translations.idiomatic: Now Song not only petitioned to send men to headquarters but invented false names and broke the ancestral institutions—can Jiang Yingkui, Tang Guoxiang, and their like be blamed for imitating him?

sentences.zh: 臣職守攸關，義不敢隱，乞特賜究正，使天下曉然知朝廷有不可幸之功、不可犯之法。

translations.literal: Your servant's duty is involved and righteousness forbids concealment; I beg that this be specially investigated and corrected, so that all under Heaven may clearly know that the court has merit that cannot be gained by luck and laws that cannot be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's office is directly concerned and duty forbids concealment; I beg special investigation and correction, so that all under Heaven may know clearly that the court has merit that cannot be seized by fortune and laws that cannot be broken.

sentences.zh: 臣雖得罪，死無所恨。

translations.literal: Though your servant should offend and die, there would be no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Though your servant should offend and die for it, he would have no regret.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，直聲震朝廷。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, his forthright voice shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, his forthright voice shook the court.

sentences.zh: 嵩父子大懼，力事彌縫。

translations.literal: The father and son Song were greatly afraid and strove to patch things over.
translations.idiomatic: Song and his son were greatly afraid and worked hard to smooth matters over.

sentences.zh: 帝責冕報復，下詔獄拷訊，斥為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor blamed Mian for retaliation, threw him into the imperial prison for interrogation under torture, and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accused Mian of retaliation, cast him into the imperial prison for torture, and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 冕既得罪，而尚書覆奏如世蕃指矣。

translations.literal: After Mian had offended, the Minister still memorialized in reply as Shifan directed.
translations.idiomatic: After Mian had been punished, the minister still memorialized in reply as Shifan directed.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，錄先朝直臣，起冕太仆少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, recording straight-speaking ministers of the previous reign, Mian was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Longqing, when straight-speaking ministers of the previous reign were honored, Mian was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，未任，卒。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother, had not taken office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was overtaken by mourning for his mother, had not assumed the post, and died.

sentences.zh: 趙錦，字元樸，余姚人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jin, style name Yuanpu, was a man of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin, whose style was Yuanpu, was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授江陰知縣，征授南京御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jiangyin and was summoned to serve as censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jiangyin, then summoned to serve as a Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 江洋有警，議設總兵官於鎮江。

translations.literal: When there was alarm on the rivers and seas, it was proposed to establish a regional commander at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When there was alarm on the rivers and seas, officials proposed establishing a regional commander at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 錦言：「小寇剽掠，不足煩重兵。」

translations.literal: Jin said: "Petty bandits who raid and plunder do not merit troubling heavy troops."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said: "Petty raiders do not warrant deploying heavy forces."

sentences.zh: 帝乃罷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then abolished the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 已，疏言：「淮兗數百里，民多流傭，乞寬租徭，簡廷臣督有司拊循。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized: "For several hundred li in Huai and Yan the people mostly hire themselves out as laborers; I beg that rents and corvée be eased and that court ministers be chosen to supervise the local officials in comforting them."
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he memorialized: "For several hundred li across Huai and Yan the people mostly hire themselves out as laborers; I beg that rents and corvée be eased and that court ministers be appointed to oversee local officials in their relief."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 軍興，民輸粟馬，得官錦衣，錦極陳不可。

translations.literal: When military campaigns arose, the people who presented grain and horses in exchange received Embroidered-Uniform Guard posts; Jin urgently memorialized that this should not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigns began, people who paid grain and horses could receive posts in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; Jin urgently argued that this should not be permitted.

sentences.zh: 尋清軍雲南。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he inspected troops in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to inspect troops in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十二年元旦，日食。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the thirty-second year there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the thirty-second year there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 錦以為權奸亂政之應，馳疏劾嚴嵩罪。

translations.literal: Jin took it as the response to powerful traitors disturbing government and hurriedly memorialized impeaching Yan Song's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took it as Heaven's response to powerful traitors corrupting government and hurriedly memorialized impeaching Yan Song's crimes.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: The gist read:
translations.idiomatic: The gist read:

sentences.zh: 臣伏見日食元旦，變異非常。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed a solar eclipse on New Year's Day—an omen most extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant observes a solar eclipse on New Year's Day—an omen most extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 又山東、徐、淮仍歲大水，四方頻地震，災不虛生。

translations.literal: Moreover Shandong, Xu, and Huai have suffered great floods year after year, and earthquakes have been frequent in all directions; calamities are not born without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shandong, Xu, and Huai have suffered great floods year after year, earthquakes have been frequent everywhere, and calamities do not arise without cause.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖高皇帝罷丞相，散其權於諸司，為後世慮至深遠矣。

translations.literal: In former times the founding Emperor Gaozu abolished the chancellor and dispersed his power among the various offices, with concern for later generations most far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the founding Emperor Taizu abolished the chancellorship and dispersed its powers among the ministries, with foresight for later ages most profound.

sentences.zh: 今之內閣，無宰相之名，而有其實，非高皇帝本意。

translations.literal: Today's Grand Secretariat has no name of chancellor yet possesses its substance—not the founding Emperor's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Grand Secretariat bears no title of chancellor yet holds its substance—this was not the founding Emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 頃夏言以貪暴之資，恣睢其間。

translations.literal: Recently Xia Yan, with his greedy and violent nature, acted arrogantly within it.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Xia Yan, greedy and violent by nature, acted arrogantly within it.

sentences.zh: 今大學士嵩又以佞奸之雄，繼之怙寵張威，竊權縱欲，事無鉅細，罔不自專。

translations.literal: Now Grand Secretary Song again, a villainous flatterer, succeeded him, relying on favor to extend his might, stealing power and indulging his desires; nothing great or small was not decided by himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now Grand Secretary Song, another villainous flatterer, has succeeded him, relying on favor to swell his power, stealing authority and indulging his desires; nothing great or small escapes his sole decision.

sentences.zh: 人有違忤，必中以禍，百司望風惕息。

translations.literal: Whoever opposed him was surely struck by disaster; the hundred offices looked to the wind and trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever opposed him was surely struck down; the hundred offices looked to the wind and trembled.

sentences.zh: 天下事未聞朝廷，先以聞政府。

translations.literal: Affairs of the realm were not first heard in the court but first heard in the government house.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of the realm were not first heard at court but first heard in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 白事之官，班候於其門；

translations.literal: Officials who came to report lined up waiting at his gate;
translations.idiomatic: Officials who came to report waited in ranks at his gate;

sentences.zh: 請求之賂，幅輳於其室。

translations.literal: gifts requested as bribes gathered in rolls at his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: bribes requested as gifts piled in rolls within his chambers.

sentences.zh: 銓司黜陟，本兵用舍，莫不承意指。

translations.literal: Dismissals and promotions in the Bureau of Personnel, appointments and removals in the Ministry of War—all followed his will.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissals and promotions in the Bureau of Personnel, appointments and removals in the Ministry of War—all followed his will.

sentences.zh: 邊臣失事，率朘削軍資納賕嵩所，無功可以受賞，有罪可以逭誅。

translations.literal: Border commanders who failed in duty mostly pared down military funds to offer bribes to Song's house; without merit one could receive rewards, and with guilt one could escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Border commanders who failed in duty mostly stripped military funds to bribe Song's household; without merit one could still be rewarded, and with guilt one could escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 至宗藩勛戚之襲封，文武大臣之贈謚，其遲速予奪，一視賂之厚薄。

translations.literal: Even the enfeoffment of imperial clansmen and meritorious kin, and posthumous titles for civil and military great ministers—their delay, grant, or denial all depended on the thickness of bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Even enfeoffments for imperial clansmen and meritorious kin, and posthumous honors for great civil and military ministers—their delay, grant, or denial all turned on the thickness of bribes.

sentences.zh: 以至希寵幹進之徒，妄自貶損。

translations.literal: Even men who curried favor and pressed for advancement falsely debased themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Even men who curried favor and pressed for advancement debased themselves without shame.

sentences.zh: 稱號不倫，廉恥掃地，有臣所不忍言者。

translations.literal: Their titles were unfitting, integrity and shame were swept to the ground—there are matters your servant cannot bear to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Their titles were unfitting and integrity was swept away—there are things your servant cannot bear to recount.

sentences.zh: 陛下天縱聖神，乾綱獨運，自以予奪由宸斷，題覆在諸司，閣臣擬旨取裁而已。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, Heaven-granted in sacred intelligence, holds the celestial regnet alone and by yourself believes that grant and denial come from the imperial decision, that memorial replies rest with the ministries, and that Grand Secretaries merely draft edicts for Your Majesty's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, Heaven-granted in sacred intelligence, holds the regnet alone and believes that grant and denial rest with the throne, memorial replies with the ministries, and that Grand Secretaries merely draft edicts for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 諸司奏稿，並承命於嵩，陛下安得知之？

translations.literal: The ministries' memorial drafts all receive orders from Song—how would Your Majesty know of them?
translations.idiomatic: The ministries' memorial drafts all take orders from Song—how would Your Majesty know of them?

sentences.zh: 今言誅，而嵩得播惡者，言剛暴而疏淺，惡易見，嵩柔佞而機深，惡難知也。

translations.literal: Now Yan is punished while Song can spread his evil: Yan was violent and shallow, his evil easy to see; Song is soft, flattering, and deep in scheming, his evil hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yan is punished while Song spreads his evil: Yan was violent and shallow, his evil easy to see; Song is soft, flattering, and deep in scheming, his evil hard to discern.

sentences.zh: 嵩窺伺逢迎之巧，似乎忠勤，諂諛側媚之態，似乎恭順。

translations.literal: Song watches and seizes the art of ingratiating compliance, seeming loyal and diligent; his fawning and sidelong flattery seem respectful and obedient.
translations.idiomatic: Song watches for chances to ingratiate himself, seeming loyal and diligent; his fawning and sidelong flattery seem respectful and obedient.

sentences.zh: 引植私人，布列要地，伺諸臣之動靜，而先發以制之，故敗露者少。

translations.literal: He brings in his private men and stations them in key posts, spying on the movements of all officials and striking first to control them, and so few of his deeds are exposed.
translations.idiomatic: He plants private men in key posts, spies on every official's movements, and strikes first to control them—so few of his deeds are exposed.

sentences.zh: 厚賂左右親信之人，凡陛下動靜意向，無不先得，故稱旨者多。

translations.literal: He lavishes bribes on those close and trusted around Your Majesty; whatever Your Majesty's movements and intentions may be, he learns them all first, and so many things accord with Your pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He lavishes bribes on those close to Your Majesty; whatever Your Majesty's movements and intentions may be, he learns them first, and so much accords with Your pleasure.

sentences.zh: 或伺聖意所註，因而行之以成其私；

translations.literal: Sometimes he watches what the sacred mind favors and acts accordingly to accomplish his private ends;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he watches what the sacred mind favors and acts accordingly to serve his private ends;

sentences.zh: 或乘事機所會，從而鼓之以肆其毒。

translations.literal: sometimes he seizes what the occasion affords and stirs it up to unleash his poison.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes he seizes what the occasion affords and stirs it up to unleash his malice.

sentences.zh: 使陛下思之，則其端本發於朝廷；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty reflects on it, the origin appears to arise from the court;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reflects on it, the origin seems to arise from court;

sentences.zh: 使天下指之，則其事不由於政府。

translations.literal: if all under Heaven points to it, the affair does not seem to come from the government house.
translations.idiomatic: if all under Heaven points to it, the affair does not seem to come from the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 幸而洞察於聖心，則諸司代嵩受其罰；

translations.literal: If fortunately Your Majesty penetrates it in the sacred mind, then the ministries bear Song's punishment in his stead;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty penetrates it in the sacred mind, the ministries bear Song's punishment in his stead;

sentences.zh: 不幸而遂傳於後世，則陛下代嵩受其愆。

translations.literal: if unhappily it is handed down to later generations, then Your Majesty bears Song's guilt in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: if unhappily it passes to later generations, Your Majesty bears Song's guilt in his stead.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈誠以嵩為賢邪？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty truly regard Song as worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty truly regard Song as worthy?

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政以來，惟恩怨是酬，惟貨賄是斂。

translations.literal: Since Song entered government, he has repaid only favors and grudges and gathered only bribes and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song entered government, he has repaid only favors and grudges and gathered only bribes and goods.

sentences.zh: 群臣憚陰中之禍，而忠言不敢直陳；

translations.literal: The hundred officials fear the disaster of secret strikes, and loyal words dare not be spoken straight;
translations.idiomatic: Officials fear the disaster of secret strikes, and loyal words dare not be spoken plainly;

sentences.zh: 四方習貪墨之風，而閭閻日以愁困。

translations.literal: the four quarters learn the ways of corruption, and the lanes and alleys grow more wretched day by day.
translations.idiomatic: the four quarters learn corruption, and the lanes and alleys grow more wretched day by day.

sentences.zh: 頃自庚戌之後，外寇陸梁。

translations.literal: Recently since the gengxu year, outer enemies have grown rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, since the gengxu year, outer enemies have grown rampant.

sentences.zh: 陛下嘗募天下之武勇以足兵，竭天下之財力以給餉，搜天下之遺逸以任將，行不次之賞，施莫測之威，以風示內外矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty once recruited the realm's martial valor to fill the armies, exhausted the realm's wealth to pay rations, searched the realm's hidden talent to appoint generals, granted out-of-turn rewards, and exercised immeasurable authority to admonish within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once recruited the realm's brave to fill the armies, exhausted the realm's wealth to pay rations, searched out hidden talent to appoint generals, granted extraordinary rewards, and exercised immeasurable authority to admonish within and without.

sentences.zh: 而封疆之臣卒未有為陛下寬宵旰憂者。

translations.literal: Yet among the border officials there has finally been none to ease Your Majesty's worries that keep you from sleep till dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among border officials there has finally been none to ease Your Majesty's worries that keep you sleepless till dawn.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣權臣行私，將吏風靡，以掊克為務，以營競為能。

translations.literal: This is because powerful ministers act for private ends, officers and troops are swept by the fashion, taking extortion as their task and factional striving as their ability.
translations.idiomatic: This is because powerful ministers act for private ends, officers and troops follow the fashion, taking extortion as their task and factional striving as their skill.

sentences.zh: 致朝廷之上，用者不賢，賢者不用；

translations.literal: It has brought it about that above the court, those employed are not worthy and the worthy are not employed;
translations.idiomatic: It has brought it about that above the court, the unworthy are employed and the worthy are passed over;

sentences.zh: 賞不當功，罰不當罪。

translations.literal: rewards do not match merit and punishments do not match crimes.
translations.idiomatic: rewards do not match merit and punishments do not match crimes.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲致太平，則群臣不足承德於左右；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to attain great peace, then the hundred officials are insufficient to bear virtue at your side;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to attain great peace, then the hundred officials are insufficient to bear virtue at your side;

sentences.zh: 欲遏戎寇，則將士不足禦侮於邊疆。

translations.literal: if you wish to check the barbarian raiders, then officers and troops are insufficient to repel insult at the borders.
translations.idiomatic: if you wish to check barbarian raiders, then officers and troops are insufficient to repel insult at the borders.

sentences.zh: 財用已竭，而外患未見底寧；

translations.literal: Resources are already exhausted, yet outer calamity has not yet seen the bottom of peace;
translations.idiomatic: Resources are already exhausted, yet outer calamity has not yet reached its end;

sentences.zh: 民困已極，而內變又虞將作。

translations.literal: The people's distress has already reached its extreme, yet there is also fear that internal turmoil may soon break out.
translations.idiomatic: The people are exhausted past endurance, and there is fear that internal upheaval may be about to erupt.

sentences.zh: 陛下躬秉至聖，憂勤萬幾，三十二年於茲矣，而天下之勢其危如此，非嵩之奸邪，何以致之？

translations.literal: Your Majesty in person holds supreme sagacity, worrying over the myriad affairs with tireless diligence—for thirty-two years it has been thus—yet the empire's situation is perilous to this degree; if not for Song's treacherous wickedness, what could have brought it to this?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty embodies supreme sagacity and has toiled over the myriad affairs of state without rest for thirty-two years now—yet the realm stands in such peril. If not for Yan Song's treachery, what could have brought us here?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下觀上天垂象，察祖宗立法之微，念權柄之不可使移，思紀綱之不可使亂，立斥罷嵩，以應天變，則朝廷清明，法紀振飭。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to observe the signs Heaven has sent down, examine the subtle intent of the ancestral founders in making law, reflect that power must not be allowed to shift, consider that statutes and discipline must not be allowed to fall into disorder, and at once dismiss and remove Song to answer Heaven's changes—then the court will be clear and bright, and law and discipline will be restored.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed Heaven's warnings, ponder the subtle purpose of our ancestors' legislation, remember that authority must not be shifted, reflect that order and discipline must not be thrown into chaos, and immediately dismiss Yan Song to answer Heaven's signs—then the court will be restored to clarity and the laws made whole again.

sentences.zh: 寇戎雖橫，臣知其不足平矣。

translations.literal: Though border enemies run rampant, your servant knows they will not be hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the frontier raiders rage unchecked, I know they will not be difficult to subdue.

sentences.zh: 當是時，楊繼盛以劾嵩得重譴，帝方蓄怒以待言者。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Jisheng, for impeaching Song, had received heavy punishment; the Emperor was storing anger waiting for those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yang Jisheng had been severely punished for impeaching Yan Song, and the Emperor was nursing his wrath, waiting for the next memorialist.

sentences.zh: 周冕爭冒功事亦下獄，而錦疏適至。

translations.literal: Zhou Mian, for disputing false claims of merit, had also been sent to prison, and Jin's memorial happened to arrive just then.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mian too had been imprisoned over his challenge to false merit claims, and Zhao Jin's memorial arrived at that very moment.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，手批其上，謂錦欺天謗君，遣使逮治，復慰諭嵩備至。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged, wrote a personal endorsement on it, saying Jin had deceived Heaven and slandered his ruler, sent agents to arrest and punish him, and again comforted and instructed Song with the utmost thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage, wrote a personal endorsement on the memorial accusing Jin of deceiving Heaven and slandering his sovereign, dispatched agents to seize him, and again comforted Yan Song with every possible kindness.

sentences.zh: 於是錦萬里就征，屢墮檻車，瀕死者數矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin traveled ten thousand li to answer the summons, repeatedly fell from the prison cart, and several times came near death.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then journeyed ten thousand li to answer the summons, repeatedly tumbling from the prison cart, and several times nearly died on the road.

sentences.zh: 既至，下詔獄拷訊，搒四十，斥為民。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was sent to the imperial prison for interrogation, given forty blows of the cangue, and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived he was cast into the imperial prison for interrogation, beaten forty strokes of the cangue, and stripped of office to live as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 父塤，時為廣西參議，亦投劾罷。

translations.literal: His father Kun, then serving as Participating Administrator of Guangxi, also submitted a resignation memorial and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kun, then Guangxi Participating Administrator, likewise submitted his resignation and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 錦家居十五年，穆宗即位，起故官。

translations.literal: Jin lived at home for fifteen years; when Muzong took the throne, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Jin remained at home for fifteen years until Muzong ascended the throne and restored him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 擢太常少卿，未上，進光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Minister of Rites; before he took up the post he was advanced to Minister of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and, before he could take up the appointment, advanced to Minister of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 江陰歲進子鱭萬斤，奏減其半。

translations.literal: Jiangyin annually presented ten thousand jin of young hairtail; he memorialized to reduce it by half.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin had been sending ten thousand jin of young hairtail each year as tribute; he memorialized to cut the levy in half.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年以右副都御史巡撫貴州，破擒叛苗龍得鲊等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief he pacified Guizhou, broke the rebels, and captured the Miao Long Dezha and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing, as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief he pacified Guizhou, routed the rebels, and captured Long Dezha of the Miao and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 宣慰安氏素桀驁，畏錦，為效命。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner of the An clan had always been fierce and insubordinate; he feared Jin and rendered loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: The An clan's Pacification Commissioner had long been proud and defiant, but he feared Jin and submitted to his command.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，歷工部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Justice and served in succession as Left and Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Minister of Justice and later served as both Left and Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘗署部事，有所爭執。

translations.literal: Once when acting in charge of ministry affairs he had disputes.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion while acting head of the ministry he became embroiled in a dispute.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年，遷南京右都御史，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he was transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing and then changed to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli he was transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, then made Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 張居正遭喪，南京大臣議疏留。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng encountered mourning, the great ministers at Nanjing deliberated a memorial to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng entered mourning, the senior ministers at Nanjing debated submitting a memorial to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 錦及工部尚書費三旸不可而止。

translations.literal: Jin and the Minister of Works Fei Sanyang opposed it and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Minister of Works Fei Sanyang objected and put a stop to the plan.

sentences.zh: 移禮部，又移吏部，俱在南京。

translations.literal: He was moved to Rites, then again to Personnel, both posts at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Rites and then to Personnel, both appointments in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 錦以居正操切，頗訾議之。

translations.literal: Jin, because Juzheng was harsh and overbearing, often criticized him in private.
translations.idiomatic: Jin found Zhang Juzheng overbearing and often spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 語聞，居正令給事中費尚伊劾錦講學談禪，妄議朝政，錦遂乞休去。

translations.literal: When word got out, Juzheng had the supervising secretary Fei Shangyi impeach Jin for lecturing on learning and Chan, and recklessly discussing state affairs; Jin thereupon begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Juzheng, he had supervising secretary Fei Shangyi impeach Jin for preaching Neo-Confucian learning and Chan doctrine and meddling rashly in state affairs; Jin then asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 居正死，給事、御史交薦，起故官。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, supervising secretaries and censors repeatedly recommended him, and he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death, supervising secretaries and censors recommended him in turn, and he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 十一年召拜左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was recalled and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 是時，方籍居正貲產。

translations.literal: At that time they were confiscating Juzheng's property.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was seizing Zhang Juzheng's estate.

sentences.zh: 錦言：「世宗籍嚴嵩家，禍延江西諸府。

translations.literal: Jin said: "In the reign of Shizong the Yan household was confiscated, and calamity spread to the various prefectures of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said: "When Shizong confiscated the Yan Song household, the harm spread across the prefectures of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 居正私藏未必逮嚴氏，若加搜索，恐貽害三楚，十倍江西民。

translations.literal: Juzheng's private hoards may not have equaled the Yan clan's, yet if searching is pressed further, I fear harm to the Three Chu regions—ten times what the people of Jiangxi suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's private wealth may not have rivaled the Yan family's, but if the search is pushed further, I fear the Three Chu will suffer tenfold what Jiangxi endured.

sentences.zh: 且居正誠擅權，非有異志。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Juzheng truly monopolized power, he harbored no different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though Juzheng did monopolize power, he harbored no treasonous ambition.

sentences.zh: 其翊戴沖聖，夙夜勤勞，中外寧謐，功亦有不容泯者。

translations.literal: In supporting and upholding the young sacred sovereign he toiled day and night; within and without the realm were tranquil—merits there are that cannot be wholly erased.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld the young sovereign and labored day and night; the realm within and without grew calm—achievements that ought not be wholly erased.

sentences.zh: 今其官蔭贈謚及諸子官職並從褫革，已足示懲，乞特哀矜，稍寬其罰。」

translations.literal: Now that his official privileges, posthumous gifts, and his sons' offices have all been stripped away, that is punishment enough; I beg special compassion and that the penalty be somewhat eased."
translations.idiomatic: His hereditary privileges, posthumous honors, and his sons' offices have already been revoked—that is punishment enough. I beg Your Majesty to show special mercy and lighten the penalty somewhat."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 二品六年滿，加太子少保，尋加兵部尚書，掌院事如故。

translations.literal: When six years at the second rank were complete, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon after he was further given Minister of War while retaining charge of the Censorate as before.
translations.idiomatic: After six years at the second rank he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon afterward he was further named Minister of War while continuing to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 錦摘陳御史封事可采者數條，請旨行之。

translations.literal: Jin selected several items from censors' sealed memorials worth adopting and requested an imperial order to carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: Jin picked out several worthwhile proposals from the censors' sealed memorials and asked that the throne order them implemented.

sentences.zh: 四川巡按雒遵憾錦，假條奏指錦為奸臣。

translations.literal: The Sichuan investigating censor Luo Zun bore a grudge against Jin and, under a pretext in memorial, pointed to Jin as a treacherous minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan investigating censor Luo Zun resented Jin and, seizing on a procedural clause, memorialized calling him a traitorous minister.

sentences.zh: 御史周希旦、給事中陳與郊不直遵，交章論列，遂調遵外任。

translations.literal: The censor Zhou Xidan and the supervising secretary Chen Yujiao did not side with Zun; they submitted memorials in turn debating the matter, and Zun was transferred to an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Xidan and supervising secretary Chen Yujiao refused to support Zun; they submitted memorials in turn refuting him, and Zun was transferred to service outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝幸山陵，再奉敕居守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited the imperial tombs, Jin was again entrusted by edict to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor went to the imperial tombs, Jin was again entrusted by edict to remain and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 其冬，以繼母喪歸。

translations.literal: That winter he returned home for his stepmother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he went home to observe mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 十九年召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was recalled and appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 年七十六矣，再辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was already seventy-six; he pleaded twice to decline, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-six years old and twice begged to decline the post, but was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 次蘇州卒。

translations.literal: He died the next stop after Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Suzhou on the journey to his post.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚端肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Junior Grand Guardian and the posthumous name Duansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Duansu.

sentences.zh: 錦始終厲清操，篤信王守仁學，而教人則以躬行為本。

translations.literal: From first to last Jin maintained stern integrity, deeply believed in Wang Yangming's learning, yet in teaching others took personal conduct as the root.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Jin held to stern integrity, was a devoted follower of Wang Yangming's teaching, and in instructing others made personal conduct the foundation.

sentences.zh: 守仁從祀孔廟，錦有力焉。

translations.literal: When Yangming was enshrined in the Confucian temple, Jin had a hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yangming was enshrined in the Confucian temple, Jin had helped bring it about.

sentences.zh: 始忤嚴嵩，得重禍。

translations.literal: At first he offended Yan Song and suffered heavy calamity.
translations.idiomatic: At first he crossed Yan Song and suffered grave punishment.

sentences.zh: 及之官貴州，道嵩裏，見嵩葬路旁，惻然憫之，屬有司護視。

translations.literal: When he went to his post in Guizhou his route passed Song's home village; he saw Song buried by the roadside, was deeply moved to pity, and ordered the local officials to protect and watch over the grave.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to Guizhou he passed Yan Song's home district, saw Song's grave by the roadside, was moved to pity, and instructed the local officials to guard it.

sentences.zh: 後忤居正罷官，居正被籍，復為營救。

translations.literal: Later he offended Juzheng and was dismissed; when Juzheng's property was confiscated, he again worked to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he offended Zhang Juzheng and was dismissed; when Juzheng's estate was seized, he again intervened on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 人以是稱錦長者。

translations.literal: People for this reason praised Jin as a man of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: For this people praised Jin as a man of true magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 吳時來，字惟修，仙居人。

translations.literal: Wu Shilai, style Weixiu, was a native of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shilai, styled Weixiu, came from Xianju.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授松江推官，攝府事。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Songjiang Prefecture and acted in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Songjiang Prefecture and served as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 倭犯境，鄉民攜妻子趨城，時來悉納之。

translations.literal: When the Wokou invaded the border, villagers carried wives and children rushing to the city; Shilai admitted them all.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates raided the district, villagers fled toward the city with wives and children in tow; Shilai took them all in.

sentences.zh: 客兵獷悍好剽掠，時來以恩結其長，犯即行法，無嘩者。

translations.literal: The guest troops were fierce and brutal and given to plunder; Shilai won over their leaders with kindness, and when any offended he applied the law at once—none made an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The mercenary troops were violent and prone to looting; Shilai bound their leaders with kindness, and when any transgressed he punished them on the spot—none dared make trouble.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城，驟雨，城壞數丈。

translations.literal: When bandits attacked the city, a sudden rainstorm broke several zhang of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits assaulted the city, a sudden downpour collapsed several zhang of the wall.

sentences.zh: 時來以勁騎扼其沖，急興版築，三日城復完，賊乃棄去。

translations.literal: Shilai with crack cavalry blocked their point of assault, urgently raised palisades and earthworks, and in three days the wall was whole again; the bandits then abandoned the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shilai blocked the breach with elite cavalry, rushed repairs, and in three days the wall was whole again; the bandits then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 劾罷兵部尚書許論、宣大總督楊順及巡按御史路楷。

translations.literal: He memorialized to dismiss the Minister of War Xu Lun, the Xuanda Grand Coordinator Yang Shun, and the investigating censor Lu Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for the dismissal of Minister of War Xu Lun, Xuanda Grand Coordinator Yang Shun, and investigating censor Lu Kai.

sentences.zh: 皆嚴嵩私人，嵩疾之甚。

translations.literal: All were Yan Song's private men; Song hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: All were Yan Song's creatures, and Song hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 會將遣使琉球，遂以命時來。

translations.literal: It happened that an envoy was about to be sent to Ryukyu, and so the appointment was given to Shilai.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was about to be dispatched to Ryukyu, and the mission was assigned to Shilai.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，時來抗章劾嵩曰：「頃陛下赫然震怒，逮治僨事邊臣，人心莫不欣快。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year Shilai submitted a defiant memorial impeaching Song, saying: "Recently Your Majesty was suddenly greatly enraged and had the border officials responsible for the failed campaign arrested and punished; in men's hearts none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year Shilai submitted a bold memorial impeaching Yan Song, saying: "Not long ago Your Majesty erupted in anger and had the border officials who bungled the campaign arrested; every heart in the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 邊臣朘軍實、饋執政，罪也。

translations.literal: The border officials drained the army's substance and made gifts to the chief minister—that is a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Those border officials hollowed out the army and paid tribute to the chief minister—that is crime enough.

sentences.zh: 執政受其饋，朋奸罔上，獨得無罪哉？

translations.literal: The chief minister received their gifts, banded with villains to deceive his sovereign—can he alone be without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the chief minister took their bribes, conspired with villains, and deceived his sovereign—can he alone go unpunished?

sentences.zh: 嵩輔政二十年，文武遷除，悉出其手。

translations.literal: Song has assisted in government for twenty years; civil and military appointments and removals all issue from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song has directed the government for twenty years; every civil and military appointment passes through his hand.

sentences.zh: 潛令子世蕃出入禁所，批答章奏。

translations.literal: He secretly had his son Shifan enter and leave the forbidden precinct, drafting replies to memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly allowed his son Shifan to enter the forbidden precinct and draft replies to memorials.

sentences.zh: 世蕃因招權示威，頤指公卿，奴視將帥，筐篚苞苴，輻輳山積，猶無饜足。

translations.literal: Shifan thereupon gathered power to display his might, ordering the public ministers with a jerk of the chin, treating generals as slaves; baskets and bundles of bribes piled up like mountains, yet still he was not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan then traded on his father's power, jerking his chin at the high ministers and treating generals as servants; gifts heaped up like mountains, yet he was never satisfied.

sentences.zh: 用所親萬寀為文選郎，方祥為職方郎，每行一事，推一官，必先稟命世蕃而後奏請。

translations.literal: He used his intimates Wan Cai as Director of the Bureau of Appointments and Fang Xiang as Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments; for every action and every promotion of an official, they first reported to Shifan for approval and only then memorialized and requested.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his favorites Wan Cai as Director of the Bureau of Appointments and Fang Xiang as Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments; for every act and every promotion they first sought Shifan's leave and only then submitted the request.

sentences.zh: 陛下但知議出部臣，豈知皆嵩父子私意哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty only knows that deliberation comes from the ministry officials—how could you know it is all the private will of Song father and son!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty believes the ministries deliberate on their own—how could you know it is all the private will of Yan Song and his son!

sentences.zh: 他不具論。

translations.literal: Other matters I do not set forth in full.
translations.idiomatic: I will not rehearse every other charge here.

sentences.zh: 如趙文華、王汝孝、張經、蔡克廉以及楊順、吳嘉會輩，或祈免死，或祈遷官，皆剝民膏以營私利，虛官帑以實權門，陛下已洞見其一二。

translations.literal: Such men as Zhao Wenhua, Wang Ruxiao, Zhang Jing, Cai Kelian, and also Yang Shun and Wu Jiahui—some begged to escape death, some begged transfer and promotion—all stripped the people's fat to serve private gain and emptied the public coffers to fill the doors of power; Your Majesty has already seen through one or two of these cases.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Zhao Wenhua, Wang Ruxiao, Zhang Jing, Cai Kelian, Yang Shun, and Wu Jiahui—some pleaded for their lives, some for promotion—all wrung the people dry for private gain and drained the treasury to enrich the powerful. Your Majesty has already seen through a few such cases.

sentences.zh: 言官如給事中袁洪愈、張墱，御史萬民英亦嘗屢及之。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials such as the supervising secretary Yuan Hongyu, Zhang Deng, and the censor Wan Minying have also repeatedly touched on these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials too—supervising secretaries Yuan Hongyu and Zhang Deng, censor Wan Minying—have raised these matters again and again.

sentences.zh: 顧多旁指微諷，無直攻嵩父子者。

translations.literal: Yet for the most part they pointed indirectly with veiled satire; none directly attacked Song father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for the most part they only hinted and circled; none struck directly at Yan Song and his son.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂除惡務本。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that in rooting out evil one must strike at the root.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that to root out evil one must strike at the root.

sentences.zh: 今邊事不振由於軍困，軍困由官邪，官邪由執政之好貨。

translations.literal: Now the border situation fails to revive because the army is exhausted; the army is exhausted because officials are corrupt; officials are corrupt because the chief minister loves gain.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier languishes because the armies are exhausted; the armies are exhausted because officials are corrupt; officials are corrupt because the chief minister is greedy.

sentences.zh: 若不去嵩父子，陛下雖宵旰憂勞，邊事終不可為也。」

translations.literal: If Song father and son are not removed, though Your Majesty toils at dawn and worries into the night, the border situation will in the end be beyond remedy."
translations.idiomatic: Unless Yan Song and his son are removed, Your Majesty may labor from dusk till dawn, yet the frontier will never be saved."

sentences.zh: 時張翀、董傳策與時來同日劾嵩。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Chong and Dong Chuance impeached Song on the same day as Shilai.
translations.idiomatic: That day Zhang Chong and Dong Chuance impeached Yan Song on the same day as Shilai.

sentences.zh: 而翀及時來皆徐階門生，傳策則階邑子，時來先又官松江，於是嵩疑階主使。

translations.literal: Chong and Shilai were both disciples of Xu Jie; Chuance was a fellow townsman of Jie; Shilai had earlier served as an official at Songjiang—thereupon Song suspected Jie had masterminded it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Shilai were both pupils of Xu Jie; Chuance was Jie's townsman; Shilai had earlier served at Songjiang—Yan Song therefore suspected Jie had orchestrated the attack.

sentences.zh: 密奏三人同日構陷，必有人主之，且時來乃憚琉球之行，借端自脫。

translations.literal: He secretly memorialized that the three men on the same day had framed a plot and must have had a patron behind them, and moreover that Shilai had dreaded the Ryukyu mission and seized the occasion to escape it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly memorialized that the three had conspired on the same day and must have had a patron, and that Shilai had dreaded the Ryukyu mission and seized on the memorial to escape it.

sentences.zh: 帝入其言，遂下三人詔獄，嚴鞫主謀者。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his words, and thereupon sent the three men to the imperial prison and rigorously interrogated them as to who had masterminded it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor believed him, sent all three to the imperial prison, and rigorously interrogated them for the mastermind.

sentences.zh: 三人瀕死不承，第言「此高廟神靈教臣為此言耳。」

translations.literal: The three, on the verge of death, would not confess, saying only, "This is the teaching of the spirit of the High Ancestor—your servant spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Near death, the three still would not confess, saying only, "The spirit of the dynastic founder taught your servant to speak thus.

sentences.zh: 主獄者乃以三人相為主使讞上。

translations.literal: Those in charge of the case then submitted a finding that the three had mutually masterminded one another.
translations.idiomatic: The interrogators then reported that the three had masterminded one another.

sentences.zh: 詔皆戍煙瘴，時來得橫州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all three exiled to miasmic regions; Shilai was sent to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent all three into miasmic exile; Shilai was banished to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，召復故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was summoned and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longqing he was recalled and restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 進工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 條上治河事宜，又薦譚綸、俞大猷、戚繼光宜用之薊鎮，專練邊兵，省諸鎮征調。

translations.literal: He listed in detail matters for governing the rivers, and also recommended Tan Lun, Yu Dayou, and Qi Jiguang as fit to be employed at the Ji garrison, there to train border troops exclusively and reduce levies from the various garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in detail on river control, and recommended Tan Lun, Yu Dayou, and Qi Jiguang for service at the Ji garrison to train frontier troops locally and spare the other commands constant redeployment.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: He was appointed to pacify and administer Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to pacify and administer Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史劉秉仁被劾且調用，時來言秉仁薦太監李芳，無大臣節，秉仁遂坐罷。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Bingren had been impeached and was about to be transferred; Shilai said Bingren had recommended the eunuch Li Fang and lacked a great minister's integrity, and Bingren thereupon was dismissed on that charge.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Bingren had been impeached and was due for transfer; Shilai said Bingren had recommended the eunuch Li Fang and lacked a statesman's dignity, and Bingren was dismissed on that account.

sentences.zh: 帝免喪既久，臨朝未嘗發言，時來上保泰九劄，報聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mourning period had long ended, yet at court audiences he had never spoken; Shilai submitted nine memorials on preserving stability, and the court acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's mourning period had long ended, yet he had never spoken at court; Shilai submitted nine memorials on preserving the throne's stability, and the court acknowledged them.

sentences.zh: 尋擢順天府丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Vice Director of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Vice Director of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，拜南京右僉都御史提督操江。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing with charge of the Yangtze naval command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longqing he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing with command of the Yangtze fleet.

sentences.zh: 移巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 將行，薦所屬有司至五十九人。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he recommended subordinate officials under him to the number of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed he recommended fifty-nine subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 給事中光懋等劾其濫舉。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Guang Mao and others impeached him for indiscriminate recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Guang Mao and others impeached him for reckless recommendations.

sentences.zh: 會高拱掌吏部，雅不喜時來，貶雲南副使。

translations.literal: It happened that Gao Gong was in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and had long disliked Shilai; Shilai was demoted to Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong then headed the Ministry of Personnel and had long disliked Shilai; Shilai was demoted to Vice Commissioner in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 復為拱門生給事中韓楫所劾，落職閑住。

translations.literal: Again he was impeached by Han Ji, a supervising secretary and Gao Gong's disciple, and was dismissed to live in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached again by Han Ji, a supervising secretary and Gao Gong's pupil, and dismissed to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十二年，始起湖廣副使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Wanli he was at last restored as Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Wanli he was at last restored as Vice Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 俄擢左通政，歷吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Left Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served in succession as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Left Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十五年拜左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 誠意伯劉世延怙惡，數抗朝令，時來劾之，下所司訊治。

translations.literal: The Earl of Cheng Yi Liu Shiyan relied on his wickedness and repeatedly defied court orders; Shilai impeached him, and he was sent down to the relevant office for interrogation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Cheng Yi, Liu Shiyan, clung to his crimes and repeatedly defied court orders; Shilai impeached him and he was sent to the appropriate office for trial.

sentences.zh: 時來初以直竄，聲振朝端。

translations.literal: At first Shilai rose through blunt remonstrance; his reputation shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: At first he shot to prominence through blunt remonstrance, and his name resounded through the court.

sentences.zh: 再遭折挫，沈淪十余年。

translations.literal: Again he met setback and reversals, sinking into obscurity for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered setback after setback and languished in obscurity for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 晚節不能自堅，委蛇執政間。

translations.literal: In his late years he could not hold himself firm, winding submissively among those in power.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he could not hold his ground and wound his way deferentially among those in power.

sentences.zh: 連為饒伸、薛敷教、王麟趾、史孟麟、趙南星、王繼光所劾，時來亦連乞休歸。

translations.literal: In succession he was impeached by Rao Shen, Xue Fujiao, Wang Linzhi, Shi Menglin, Zhao Nanxing, and Wang Jiguang; Shilai also repeatedly begged to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached in turn by Rao Shen, Xue Fujiao, Wang Linzhi, Shi Menglin, Zhao Nanxing, and Wang Jiguang, and Shilai too repeatedly asked to resign and go home.

sentences.zh: 未出都，卒。

translations.literal: Before he had left the capital, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left the capital, he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚忠恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Zhongke (Loyal and Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Zhongke (Loyal and Respectful).

sentences.zh: 尋為禮部郎中於孔兼所論，奪謚。

translations.literal: Soon Yu Kongjian, a bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, impeached him, and his posthumous name was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yu Kongjian of the Ministry of Rites impeached him, and his posthumous name was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 張翀，字子儀，柳州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, style Ziyi, was a native of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, style Ziyi, was a native of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 疾嚴嵩父子亂政，抗章劾之。

translations.literal: Grieved that Yan Song father and son threw government into disorder, he submitted a defiant memorial impeaching them.
translations.idiomatic: Outraged that Yan Song and his son were throwing government into chaos, he submitted a defiant memorial impeaching them.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: The gist ran:
translations.idiomatic: The gist ran:

sentences.zh: 竊見大學士嵩貴則極人臣，富則甲天下。

translations.literal: I have observed that Grand Secretary Song in rank reaches the apex of subjects and in wealth surpasses all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Grand Secretary Song in rank has reached the summit of subjecthood and in wealth surpasses all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 子為侍郎，孫為錦衣、中書，賓客滿朝班，親姻盡朱紫。

translations.literal: His son is a vice minister; his grandsons hold posts in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the Secretariat Drafters; guests fill the court ranks, and kinsmen by marriage all wear purple and scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: His son is a vice minister; his grandsons serve in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and as Secretariat drafters; his clients pack the court ranks, and every marriage tie wears purple or scarlet.

sentences.zh: 犬馬尚知報主，乃嵩則不然。

translations.literal: Even dogs and horses know to repay their master—yet Song is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Even dogs and horses know how to repay their master—yet Song does not.

sentences.zh: 臣試以邊防、財賦、人才三大政言之。

translations.literal: Your servant will try to speak of this through the three great policies: frontier defense, finance, and talent.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant will address this through the three great policies: frontier defense, finance, and talent.

sentences.zh: 國家所恃為屏翰者，邊鎮也。

translations.literal: What the state relies upon as its screen and rampart is the frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: What the state relies on as its screen and rampart are the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政，文武將吏率由賄進。

translations.literal: Since Song entered the Grand Secretariat, civil and military officers and generals have mostly advanced through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song took up the Grand Secretariat, civil and military officers and generals have advanced chiefly through bribery.

sentences.zh: 其始不核名實，但通關節，即與除授。

translations.literal: At first they did not verify name and reality—only pass through connections, and office was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At first they did not examine merit or credentials—only pull strings, and appointment followed.

sentences.zh: 其後不論功次，但勤問遺，即被超遷。

translations.literal: Afterward they did not weigh merit and seniority—only diligently send gifts, and one was promoted ahead of others.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they did not weigh merit or seniority—only keep the gifts flowing, and promotion came out of turn.

sentences.zh: 托名修邊建堡，覆軍者得蔭子，濫殺者得轉官。

translations.literal: Under the pretext of repairing the frontier and building forts, those who lost armies had sons ennobled, and those who killed recklessly were transferred and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the pretext of repairing the frontier and building forts, commanders who lost armies saw their sons ennobled, and those who killed recklessly were transferred and promoted.

sentences.zh: 公肆詆欺，交相販鬻。

translations.literal: They openly slandered and deceived, buying and selling offices one for another.
translations.idiomatic: They openly slandered and deceived one another, trading offices back and forth.

sentences.zh: 而祖宗二百年防邊之計盡廢壞矣。

translations.literal: Thus the forefathers' two-hundred-year plan for frontier defense was utterly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the forefathers' two-hundred-year plan for frontier defense was utterly ruined.

sentences.zh: 戶部歲發邊餉，本以贍軍。

translations.literal: Each year the Ministry of Revenue disbursed frontier pay, originally to support the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Ministry of Revenue disbursed frontier pay—originally to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政，朝出度支之門，暮入奸臣之府。

translations.literal: Since Song came to power, funds left the revenue office in the morning and by evening entered the villain's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song came to power, silver leaves the revenue office in the morning and by evening enters the villain's mansion.

sentences.zh: 輸邊者四，饋嵩者六。

translations.literal: Four parts went to the frontier; six parts were presented to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Four parts reach the frontier; six parts are presented to Song.

sentences.zh: 臣每過長安街，見嵩門下無非邊鎮使人。

translations.literal: Whenever Your servant passes Chang'an Street, I see at Song's gate nothing but envoys from frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I pass Chang'an Street, I see at Song's gate nothing but envoys from the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 未見其父，先饋其子。

translations.literal: Before seeing the father, they first present gifts to the son.
translations.idiomatic: Before they see the father, they first present gifts to the son.

sentences.zh: 未見其子，先饋家人。

translations.literal: Before seeing the son, they first present gifts to the household staff.
translations.idiomatic: Before they see the son, they first present gifts to the household staff.

sentences.zh: 家人嚴年富已逾數十萬，嵩家可知。

translations.literal: The retainer Yan Nian's wealth already exceeds several hundred thousand—Song's household may be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: The retainer Yan Nian's wealth already exceeds several hundred thousand taels—Song's household may be imagined from that.

sentences.zh: 私藏充溢，半屬軍儲；

translations.literal: Private hoards overflow; half of it is army provisions;
translations.idiomatic: Private hoards overflow; half of it is army provisions;

sentences.zh: 邊卒凍餒，不保朝夕。

translations.literal: Frontier soldiers freeze and starve, not assured of the morrow.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier soldiers freeze and starve, with no assurance of the morrow.

sentences.zh: 而祖宗二百年豢養之軍盡耗弱矣。

translations.literal: Thus the army the forefathers nurtured for two hundred years was utterly drained and weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the army the forefathers nurtured for two hundred years was utterly drained and weakened.

sentences.zh: 邊防既隳。

translations.literal: Frontier defense was already in ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier defense was already in ruins.

sentences.zh: 邊儲既虛，使人才足供陛下用，猶不足憂也。

translations.literal: Frontier stores were already empty—if talent were enough to serve Your Majesty, there would still be no cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier stores are already empty—if talent alone were enough to serve Your Majesty, there would still be little to fear.

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政，藐蔑名器，私營囊橐。

translations.literal: Since Song came to power, he has scorned offices and titles and privately filled his purse.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song came to power, he has scorned offices and titles while privately filling his purse.

sentences.zh: 世蕃以狙獪資，倚父虎狼之勢，招權罔利，獸攫烏鈔。

translations.literal: Shifan, with his cunning and treachery, leaning on his father's tiger-and-wolf power, drew power and seized profit—beasts clawing and crows snatching.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan, cunning and treacherous by nature, leans on his father's tiger-and-wolf power to seize authority and profit—beasts clawing, crows snatching.

sentences.zh: 無恥之徒，絡繹奔走，靡然成風，有如狂易。

translations.literal: Shameless men hurried to his door in an unbroken stream until it became a prevailing wind, like madness.
translations.idiomatic: Shameless men hurried to his door in an unbroken stream until it became the prevailing wind, like a fever in the land.

sentences.zh: 而祖宗二百年培養之人才盡敗壞矣。

translations.literal: Thus talent the forefathers cultivated for two hundred years was utterly corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the talent the forefathers cultivated for two hundred years was utterly corrupted.

sentences.zh: 夫嵩險足以傾人，詐足以惑世，辨足以亂政，才足以濟奸。

translations.literal: Song's malice suffices to overturn men, his deceit to bewilder the age, his eloquence to disorder government, and his talent to advance villainy.
translations.idiomatic: Song's malice is enough to overturn men, his deceit enough to bewilder the age, his eloquence enough to disorder government, and his talent enough to advance villainy.

sentences.zh: 附己者加諸膝，異己者墜之淵。

translations.literal: Those who attached to him he drew to his knee; those unlike him he dropped into the abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sided with him he drew to his knee; those who differed from him he cast into the abyss.

sentences.zh: 箝天下口使不敢言，而其惡日以恣。

translations.literal: He clamped the mouths of all under Heaven so none dared speak, while his wickedness grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: He clamped shut the mouths of all under Heaven so none dared speak, while his wickedness grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 此忠義之士，所以搤腕憤激，懷深長之憂者也。

translations.literal: This is why men of loyalty and righteousness clench their wrists in fury and harbor deep, lasting grief.
